items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Connect an OpenZilo ring from Python, read device information, recordings and motion data, and integrate them into your application. Public APIs are provided by the openzilo package; the CLI is installed with the SDK.

items.title: OpenZilo platform
items.text:
OpenZilo is an open development platform for building always-available AI experiences with wearable hardware.

Starting with smart rings, OpenZilo provides developers with hardware, firmware, SDKs, and reference applications for connecting voice, gestures, physiological signals, AI agents, computers, robots, and the physical world.

This repository contains the Python SDK and CLI for scanning and connecting to an OpenZilo ring, reading device information, downloading recordings, converting Speex or mono/stereo Opus to WAV, and receiving IMU and gesture events.

Run openzilo device use to scan and save a default ring, then openzilo shell for an interactive terminal. Device commands also accept OPENZILO_ADDRESS or --address. Use sensor-stream --seconds 10 --output imu.jsonl for timed IMU capture. See the Chinese CLI guide; remote recording requires matching extended firmware.

Run uvx --from git+https://github.com/ziloai/OpenZilo.git openzilo shell to start the interactive terminal directly from GitHub. See the CLI guide.

It documents protocol v4 on firmware V2.001.0002.0000. Check device behavior on your own hardware.

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
You need uv, Python 3.10+ (uv can install it), and a BLE adapter. On Linux, you also need BlueZ and Bluetooth access.

Install the device CLI from GitHub:

uv tool install git+https://github.com/ziloai/OpenZilo.git
openzilo scan --timeout 10
openzilo info --address AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF

Replace the example address with one returned by scan. To use the SDK in your uv project, run uv add git+https://github.com/ziloai/OpenZilo.git. Without uv, use python -m pip install git+https://github.com/ziloai/OpenZilo.git.

In Python:

import asyncio
import openzilo as sdk


async def main() -> None:
    async with sdk.OpenZiloClient(address="AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF") as ring:
        info = await sdk.get_system_info(ring)
        print(info.model, info.firmware_version, info.battery_percent)


asyncio.run(main())

See the examples for audio download and IMU streaming.

For live mono/stereo PCM, install uv add "openzilo[pcm] @ git+https://github.com/ziloai/OpenZilo.git" and consume sdk.open_live_audio_stream(ring) with async with / async for. It yields LiveAudioStart, 20 ms LivePcmFrame blocks (16 kHz s16le, with the configured channel count), then a verified LiveAudioEnd. Slow consumers fail explicitly; leaving the context stops an unfinished capture and attempts unsubscribe. This path uses PyAV and does not need an ffmpeg executable. See the live PCM example and live audio guide. Use output="opus" to consume original packets with only the base SDK.

Install ffmpeg if you need Speex/Opus-to-WAV conversion. audio-clear deletes recordings from the device and requires --yes.

items.title: Contributing
items.text: Contributions to the SDK, examples and documentation are welcome. Keep changes focused and preserve compatibility for the public API in openzilo.__all__. If an API must change, explain its impact and migration steps.

items.title: Code changes
items.text:
Keep code in the module responsible for the feature and export public APIs from openzilo. For protocol or parser changes, add hardware-free tests and update relevant examples and documentation.

Run these checks from the repository:

uv sync --locked
uv run python -m compileall src
uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
uv run openzilo --help

Use uv add or uv remove to change dependencies, and commit the updated uv.lock. For hardware-dependent changes, describe the applicable firmware and device in the PR.

items.title: Documentation changes
items.text: Write documentation in Markdown. State device, firmware and SDK requirements explicitly; a protocol version alone does not establish feature support.

items.title: Submission contents
items.text:
Use placeholder addresses in examples. Remove real device addresses, serial numbers, CPUIDs, private recordings and credentials before submitting. Do not include device captures, generated audio, firmware, APKs or CAD files in SDK changes.

Software and documentation contributions use MPL-2.0. Hardware designs published in their own repository use its hardware license. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in the security policy.

items.title: Security policy
items.text:
Please report suspected security vulnerabilities privately to openzilo@ziloring.com. Do not open a public issue for an unpatched vulnerability.

Include affected version, reproduction details, and potential impact. Redact device MAC addresses, serial numbers, CPUIDs, and recorded audio before sharing logs. We will acknowledge receipt and coordinate disclosure when a fix is available.

items.title: OpenZilo SDK architecture and data flow
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Connection requirements

Your computer needs Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE). The SDK communicates with the ring through NUS and supports protocol v4.

This page explains BLE and recording processing in the current SDK. See the ring guide for device operations and feature requirements for firmware requirements.

It covers receiving data, downloading files and producing WAV. Function signatures and examples are in the API index; commands and fields are in the protocol reference.
path: OpenZilo SDK architecture and data flow

items.title: Module organization
items.text:
Applications import public names from openzilo.__all__. Implementation modules are private and underscore-prefixed:

Module Responsibility _errors Exceptions and device error codes. _protocol V4 headers, CRC, command numbers and binary I/O. _transport Bleak-based NUS discovery, connection and chunked writes. _client OpenZiloClient request matching and packet dispatch. _tasks Asyncio deadline and background callback helpers. _device Scanning, connections, system information, logs and time synchronization. _ota Application firmware updates. _compatibility Feature discovery, interface version and recording parameter checks. _recording Remote recording, status and configuration. _identity, _version SDK version and source checksum. _audio Stored recording queries, download and automatic reception. _live_audio Live recording subscription and reception. _codec Speex, OP2C and WAV conversion. _pcm Optional stateful PyAV Opus decoding and PCM framing, independent of BLE. _sensor IMU reporting and motion events. _cli python -m openzilo CLI.

_errors and _protocol do not depend on BLE. _codec is also independent of connections and can process files offline.
path: OpenZilo SDK architecture and data flow

items.title: Live audio streams
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

open_live_audio_stream() manages subscription and cleanup with an async context, yielding START, audio frames and END for one recording. Context entry confirms subscription; users still trigger recording with the button. One task reads the stream. Context exit aborts unfinished reception and attempts unsubscribe.

BLE notifications -> bounded _PacketInbox -> background receiver: session, sequence and offset checks
                                        -> Opus events
                                        -> optional stateful decode/resample -> 20 ms PCM
                                        -> bounded event queue -> application async for

The receiver exclusively owns audio operations, excluding downloads, other receivers and OTA. Client receive_queue_size controls the raw queue (default 256); stream queue_size controls output events (default 64). Both report overflow errors instead of dropping data silently. Pausing local consumption cannot stop the ring from transmitting.

The optional pcm extra supplies PyAV. Each recording creates a stateful decoder/resampler and processes packets sequentially in a worker thread. Output is 16 kHz signed 16-bit little-endian PCM, 320 samples per channel per frame. Channel count follows the recording, with stereo interleaved L/R. After valid END, the resampler drains and total samples are checked. No per-packet files or ffmpeg processes are created.

Streaming does not accumulate an entire recording. receive_live_audio_file() reads the same validated Opus events and assembles OP2C. Only a checked END establishes completeness; live-only data lost after an error cannot be recovered from flash.
path: OpenZilo SDK architecture and data flow

items.title: From BLE notifications to SDK APIs
items.text:
Ring Nordic UART Service
  ↓  BLE notifications / characteristic writes
NusClient                 scan, connect, subscribe, chunk writes
  ↓
PacketStream              reconstruct v4 packets, check header and CRC
  ↓
OpenZiloClient            dispatch responses and events by command
  ↓
get_system_info() / download_audio_file() / wait_sensor_data() ...

NusClient uses bleak and connects by address, without relying on advertising names. NUS RX writes contain at most 20 bytes per chunk; system MTU negotiation remains enabled. Ring TX notifications have no matching 20-byte guarantee.

PacketStream.feed() accepts arbitrary notification sizes, including partial or consecutive packets. It uses body_length to extract packets and skips bytes before the magic marker. Invalid headers, CRC or lengths raise ProtocolError. Bodies are limited to 5120 bytes.

OpenZiloClient maintains per-command queues. request() serializes calls expecting the same response, drains stale queued packets, sends and waits. wait_for_command() receives events such as 0x0605. Long-lived listeners use add_packet_handler(), as time synchronization does. Queue capacity defaults to 256; overflow clears backlog and raises ProtocolError. Callback-only handlers use queue_packets=False for exclusive delivery without queue copies. BLE disconnect during waits raises TransportError.
path: OpenZilo SDK architecture and data flow

items.title: Protocol v4 packet boundaries
items.text:
The fixed header is 11 bytes:

magic:u8=0x3F | version:u16=4 | command:u16 | body_length:u32 | body_crc:u16 | body

Header and body integers are big-endian. CRC16 covers body only and is 0 for an empty body. BinaryReader and BinaryWriter handle these fields. Speex frame lengths are separate two-byte little-endian file fields, not protocol headers. See the protocol reference.
path: OpenZilo SDK architecture and data flow

items.title: Recording formats
items.text:
Firmware version

OP2C mono/stereo Opus recordings are available starting with V2.001.0002.0001. Decoding existing Speex files does not require a firmware upgrade.

Firmware V2.001.0002.0000 stores consecutive Speex frames; V2.001.0002.0001 stores mono/stereo OP2C. Firmware upgrades do not convert existing files, so both can coexist. The SDK detects encoding from contents, not firmware versions or filename extensions.

Each Speex frame has a two-byte little-endian payload length:

[length:u16 little-endian][Speex payload:length bytes]
[length:u16 little-endian][Speex payload:length bytes]
...

For example, 14 00 means 20 payload bytes. Read each length rather than splitting at fixed 20-byte boundaries. Speex Wideband frames contain 320 mono samples at 16 kHz (20 ms). Individual packets are limited to 540 bytes; default decoded PCM is 16 kHz mono 16-bit.

OP2C starts with a 12-byte little-endian header followed by length-prefixed Opus packets:

magic:"OP2C" | version:u16=1 | channels:u16=1 or 2 | sample_rate:u16=16000 | frame_samples:u16=320
[length:u16 little-endian][Opus payload:length bytes]
...

Each Opus packet carries 20 ms at 16 kHz with the header's channels, in 1–100 bytes. A recording has at most 3000 packets (60 seconds), without trailing padding or terminators.

Join 0x0505.data by frame_offset. The file data excludes device file-management metadata; AudioFileInfo.data_size is its byte count. For Speex, data starts with the first length field. SDK .bin output preserves the original format for later decoding.
path: OpenZilo SDK architecture and data flow

items.title: Recording transfers
items.text:
Entry point Device interaction SDK API Normal extraction 0x0503 → 0x0504 metadata, repeated 0x0506 → 0x0505 by offset, then 0x0507 → 0x0508 download_audio_file(..., quick=False) Fast extraction 0x0509 → 0x0504, then consecutive 0x0505 download_audio_file(..., quick=True), default V2.001.0002.0000 post-save push Consecutive 0x0505, without initial 0x0504 receive_auto_audio_file() V2.001.0002.0001 post-save notification Device sends 0x050A; SDK downloads normally receive_auto_audio_file() Live recording Subscribe 0x050D → 0x050E; button recording sends 0x050F, consecutive 0x0510, then 0x0511 receive_live_audio_file()

Each 0x0505 has a file index and offset. Assembly skips duplicate overlap. Gaps or timeouts in fast transfer trigger 0x0506 recovery; more than three unsuccessful recovery attempts raise ProtocolError. Output is truncated to data_size. Device data chunks are at most 4096 bytes; SDK bodies are limited to 5120.

Legacy push happens after saving, with no initial extraction request. receive_auto_audio_file() selects the first frame's index and returns (file_index, raw_audio). For missing data it queries metadata, checks file length and recovers by offset, failing rather than returning incomplete audio.

The 0x050A save notification carries a file index. The SDK performs normal extraction and sends 0x0507 to release the file, including on errors.

Live-only audio is not stored and cannot be retransmitted. Simultaneous saving permits downloading a completed device copy. Live reception validates session, sequence, offsets and END counts, rejecting incomplete audio. It packages Opus as OP2C for the same decoding path used by downloaded files.

Connect before automatic transmission begins. receive_auto_audio_file(), download_audio_file() and read_audio_frame() share 0x0505; concurrent use is rejected with ProtocolError. If push was missed, query the count and download by index.
path: OpenZilo SDK architecture and data flow

items.title: From Speex / Opus to WAV
items.text:
Speex: .bin -> read frame lengths -> Speex payload -> temporary Ogg Speex
            -> ffmpeg s16le PCM -> add RIFF/WAV header -> .wav
OP2C:  .bin -> validate header and packet lengths -> Opus -> temporary Ogg Opus
            -> ffmpeg 16 kHz mono/stereo s16le PCM -> add RIFF/WAV header -> .wav

OP2C decoding follows its header's channel count; a caller-supplied pcm_config cannot override it. Missing ffmpeg raises OpusDecoderUnavailable on the Opus path.

save_audio_bundle() writes raw .bin first, then attempts WAV. The raw file survives missing ffmpeg or decode failure, reported as SpeexDecoderUnavailable, OpusDecoderUnavailable or AudioDecodeError.

build_playable_audio() returns existing WAV unchanged and recognizes Ogg Speex or raw Speex without lengths. source_type may be wav, ogg-speex, packet-speex or raw-speex; OP2C returns opus-mono or opus-stereo. Only raw-Speex fallback uses quality and bits_size: quality 3 estimates 20-byte frames, while explicit bits_size overrides that estimate.

For legacy 1026-byte outer blocks, pass allow_framed_blocks=True. Low-level parse_packetized_speex_stream() allows them by default; higher-level decoding and saving APIs require explicit opt-in.

build_ogg_speex() constructs a temporary container with speex-1.2.1, Wideband, 16 kHz mono, 320 samples per frame, one frame per packet, and vendor openzilo-python. Granule position advances by 320 per packet. ffmpeg emits s16le; build_wav_from_pcm() adds a 44-byte header. If one packet decodes to multiple evenly sized frames, normalize_decoded_speex_pcm() retains only the first. Intermediate Ogg files are not saved separately by default.

File/data Content Directly playable? Device .bin Length-prefixed Speex or OP2C No .spx / .ogg Speex in Ogg With a Speex-capable player s16le PCM Unwrapped 16-bit samples Requires sample rate and channels .wav PCM with RIFF/WAV header Yes

Changing extensions does not convert formats. Extract, wrap and decode the Speex or Opus packets to produce WAV.
path: OpenZilo SDK architecture and data flow

items.title: IMU and motion events
items.text:
Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 starts capture and reports on start_sensor_report(), and stops capture on stop_sensor_report() or disconnect. Subscribe again after reconnecting. Firmware V2.001.0002.0000 needs gesture mode first and can retain local detection after BLE reports stop.

The SDK accepts two successful 0x0605 formats:

  • Single sample: error_code:u16 + sequence:u32 + timestamp_ms:u32 + six_axes:i16*6, 22 bytes.
  • Batch: error_code:u16 + sequence_start:u32 + frame_count:u16 + sample_size:u16 + samples, 10 + 16*N bytes.

Both return SensorDataBatch, with frame_count=1 for single-sample input. The event layouts below are retained in V2.001.0002.0000 and V2.001.0002.0001.

Command Event Body 0x0701 Physical double tap timestamp_ms:u32, milliseconds since boot 0x0703 Double button press u32 device seconds; SDK retains timestamp_ms 0x0704 Single button press u32 device seconds; SDK retains timestamp_ms

Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 detects taps using IMU data enabled by subscription, and single presses (0x0704) no longer switch modes. Firmware V2.001.0002.0000 detects taps in gesture mode and uses single presses for mode switching. LEDs are local indicators without an SDK query.

Restart reports after reconnection. Local capture restoration depends on firmware.
path: OpenZilo SDK architecture and data flow

items.title: Debugging checklist
items.text:
• Unplayable .bin: use save_audio_bundle() for raw Speex/OP2C conversion and check ffmpeg installation.
  • ffmpeg format error: check file framing, offset-based assembly, and that no protocol fields were mixed into audio. Speex starts with its two-byte length; OP2C starts with its header.
  • No 0x0605: confirm successful 0x0602 after starting reports. Enter gesture mode first only on firmware requiring it.
  • Consecutive 0x0505 without 0x0504: this is post-save push; use receive_auto_audio_file().

When firmware or protocols change, compare device behavior, src/openzilo/ and the protocol reference, then update the SDK guide and this page.
path: OpenZilo SDK architecture and data flow

items.title: Command-line guide
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Install and run device commands from GitHub. Enable Bluetooth and keep the ring nearby and connectable.

items.title: Run directly with uvx
items.text:
Fetch the CLI from GitHub and enter the interactive shell without setting up a project environment:

uvx --from git+https://github.com/ziloai/OpenZilo.git openzilo shell

uvx manages an isolated environment automatically. Device operations require Bluetooth and OS access permissions. Inside the shell, select a ring and run commands:

openzilo> device use
openzilo> info
openzilo> doctor
openzilo> exit

For frequent use, install the command from GitHub, then invoke openzilo directly:

uv tool install git+https://github.com/ziloai/OpenZilo.git
openzilo shell

The examples below use the installed openzilo command. You can also enter subcommands inside the shell. Device selection is stored in the user configuration directory and survives tool environment changes.

To pin a branch, tag or commit, append @REF to the GitHub URL:

uvx --from git+https://github.com/ziloai/OpenZilo.git@REF openzilo shell

Replace REF with the required revision. Refresh the GitHub tool environment with uvx --refresh --from git+https://github.com/ziloai/OpenZilo.git openzilo shell. See the official uv tools guide.

items.title: First use
items.text:
# Scan and select the default device by number
openzilo device use

# Read device information, battery and firmware version
openzilo info

# Enter the interactive shell
openzilo shell

With a known address, run openzilo device use AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF; on macOS use the scanned UUID. Saving an address does not connect immediately. openzilo scan lists nearby devices without changing the default.

The default device is stored in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/openzilo/config.json, or ~/.config/openzilo/config.json when XDG is unset. The file contains only the device address and is created with current-user read/write permissions. Do not commit real device settings. OPENZILO_CONFIG selects another file.

Address precedence: command --address, then shell --address, then OPENZILO_ADDRESS, then the saved default. scan ignores the default and uses its own --address filter.

openzilo device show
openzilo device forget
openzilo info --address AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF

device forget deletes local configuration only; it neither modifies the ring nor clears environment variables. Use it to reset damaged configuration, or run device use ADDRESS again.

items.title: Interactive shell
items.text:
Inside shell, enter subcommands without the openzilo prefix:

openzilo> info
openzilo> audio-count
openzilo> audio-config
openzilo> audio-record recordings/test.wav --seconds 5 --channels 1 --bitrate 16000
openzilo> audio-status
openzilo> sensor-stream --seconds 10 --output captures/imu.jsonl
openzilo> help audio-record
openzilo> exit

help lists commands; help COMMAND shows arguments. Each device command connects and disconnects independently, so the shell does not hold BLE continuously. device use changes the saved default, but an initial shell --address override remains effective. Command errors return to the prompt. Ctrl+C cancels and exits; Ctrl+D or exit closes the shell.

items.title: Recording and configuration
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

Remote start, stop, status and settings require firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later. They are absent from V2.001.0002.0000. See recording control.

# Read settings; Q8 gain 256 means 1x
openzilo audio-config
openzilo audio-config --channels 2 --bitrate 32000 --gain-left-q8 256 --gain-right-q8 256

# Record five seconds remotely, wait for saving, download and create playable audio
openzilo audio-record recordings/test.wav --seconds 5

# Stream while retaining a device copy
openzilo audio-record recordings/live.wav --destination both --seconds 5

# Query status; use the actual session_id to stop or discard
openzilo audio-status
openzilo audio-stop 123
openzilo audio-stop 123 --cancel

123 is illustrative; use the session ID returned by status. A stop acknowledgment does not confirm saving; the command waits for final state. If START times out, query audio-status before another START.

Configuration survives reconnection and resets on reboot. audio-record defaults to flash storage and stopping on disconnect; unspecified settings retain device values. --max-duration-ms is the device limit (20–60000 ms in 20 ms steps); --seconds is how long the CLI waits before requesting stop (0.02–60 seconds). A shorter device limit ends recording earlier.

Converting Speex/Opus to WAV requires an ffmpeg executable; specify it with --ffmpeg /path/to/ffmpeg. Legacy recordings can be received after a button recording or downloaded:

openzilo audio-receive recordings/button.wav
openzilo audio-download 0 recordings/saved.wav
openzilo audio-decode recordings/raw.bin recordings/decoded.wav

audio-live waits for a button-triggered recording; whether flash retains a copy depends on configuration. audio-clear --yes permanently deletes every recording and requires explicit --yes.

items.title: Live audio
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

openzilo audio-live recordings/live.wav

items.title: IMU and other operations
items.text:
# One JSON batch per line, with sequence_start, frame_count, sample_size and samples
openzilo sensor-stream --seconds 10 --output captures/imu.jsonl

# Print to the terminal or pipe stdout to another program
openzilo sensor-stream --seconds 5

openzilo connect
openzilo time-sync --seconds 30
openzilo log-storage
openzilo log-read 0 0 128 --text
openzilo ota-update --help

Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 starts IMU directly; V2.001.0002.0000 requires gesture mode first. At the time limit, error or cancellation, the command attempts to stop reports and disconnect. File output overwrites its path, creating parent directories; batches already written remain after failure. Values remain in protocol units; see the IMU guide.

Connection commands accept --scan-timeout and --connect-timeout. Errors go to stderr and exit with 1; argument errors with 2; Ctrl+C with 130. Interactive command errors return to the prompt.

items.title: Compatibility diagnostics
items.text: openzilo --version shows the SDK version. openzilo device capabilities shows features, recording limits and information source. openzilo doctor also shows the SDK source checksum and audio dependencies. Remote recording, live audio, IMU and OTA query capabilities before running; support is checked from the response, not firmware version ordering. See compatibility.

items.title: Software IMU calibration
items.text:
Use openzilo imu-calibrate accel for six-face accelerometer calibration in the charging case, quick for stationary gyro calibration outside the case, or full for both stages. Independent validation precedes atomic local saving. show reads the local file; reset deletes it. sensor-stream --calibrated --seconds 10 explicitly applies the matching profile, outputs g / deg/s and marks the corrected components. Default raw streaming is unchanged. No calibration parameters are sent to the ring. See the software calibration specification.

Inspect and verify all signed OTA ZIP metadata offline:

openzilo ota-inspect firmware.ota.zip --public-key trusted-signing-public.pem --json

items.title: SDK and firmware compatibility
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Available since SDK v0.6.1

connect_ring() discovers features automatically. When using OpenZiloClient, call get_device_capabilities() explicitly.

A successful connection establishes BLE communication. Remote recording, live audio, IMU and firmware updates additionally require a compatible device interface.

items.title: Recommended connection method
items.text:
connect_ring() discovers supported features by default. Inspect ring.capabilities after connecting:

import asyncio
import openzilo as sdk

ADDRESS = "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"

async def main():
    ring = await sdk.connect_ring(address=ADDRESS, auto_time_sync=True)
    try:
        capabilities = ring.capabilities
        print("Firmware:", capabilities.firmware_version)
        print("Model:", capabilities.model)
        if capabilities.supports("recording_control"):
            print(await sdk.get_audio_recording_config(ring))
    finally:
        await ring.disconnect()

asyncio.run(main())

With async with sdk.OpenZiloClient(...), run this before those operations:

capabilities = await sdk.get_device_capabilities(ring)

CLI remote recording, live audio, IMU and OTA commands query features automatically. Basic information, logs, existing-file downloads and time replies do not depend on discovery.

items.title: Where support information comes from
items.text:
Release builds V2.001.0002.0000 and V2.001.0002.0001 have no feature-discovery command. The SDK uses a built-in profile for exact versions it recognizes. This page explains SDK discovery and error handling; the minimum firmware version for a usage is stated directly in its feature section.

DeviceCapabilities.source identifies the source:

Value Meaning device The device returned a feature list; the SDK also checked the model and firmware version. legacy_profile The old firmware returned no list, so the SDK selected a built-in profile by exact firmware version and model. unknown No feature list or matching built-in profile is available.

The current built-in profile matches model Open Zilo and firmware V2.001.0002.0001-prod-7fd1dfc9. A shared version prefix does not select it. Discovery timeout means no response was obtained, not necessarily that a feature is absent.

items.title: Check feature availability
items.text:
Use capabilities.supports("FEATURE_NAME"). Common feature names:

Feature Purpose recording_control Start, stop and configure recordings. live_audio Receive live audio. imu Receive accelerometer and gyroscope data. key_events Receive button events. double_tap Receive physical tap events. ota Update application firmware.

The SDK also checks the interface major version. For example, imu/2 starts capture on subscription. An older interface requiring gesture mode is not interchangeable just because the feature name matches.

Recording settings are checked against device channel, bitrate, gain, duration and output limits. Continuing on disconnect requires flash storage or simultaneous saving, not live-only output.

items.title: Handle errors
items.text:
Exception Common cause Action CompatibilityError Feature absent, interface version mismatch or recording settings outside limits Inspect features and limits; adjust the call or choose compatible firmware. DeviceError Device rejected a command, such as during another operation Inspect error_code, finish conflicting operations and retry. TimeoutError No response before the deadline Check the connection and reconnect before discovery. After START timeout, query recording state before retrying. ProtocolError Missing fields or inconsistent data Record SDK and firmware versions plus the error and report it.

Results last for the current connection only and are cleared on disconnect. They are refreshed after OTA reconnection. Reconnect before retrying discovery after a failed legacy query.

items.title: Inspect diagnostics
items.text:
uv run openzilo --version
uv run openzilo device capabilities
uv run openzilo doctor

device capabilities outputs features and recording limits as JSON. doctor also reports the SDK version, source checksum and PyAV availability. Include these when reporting issues, after removing addresses, serial numbers and private audio.

items.title: Advanced connection options
items.text:
allow_unverified_features=True permits feature calls when discovery is unknown, for applications that already know the interface. It does not override an explicit version mismatch. The CLI equivalent is --allow-unverified-features.

negotiate_capabilities=False disables automatic discovery; the caller must establish compatibility. This matches the default low-level OpenZiloClient connection behavior.

items.title: Wire fields
items.text: For custom client implementations, see capability discovery messages. Ordinary applications can use the SDK APIs above.

items.title: Features and version requirements
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Check the ring's firmware version and supported features before choosing an API. The SDK, firmware and communication protocol have separate version numbers.

items.title: Check versions and features
items.text:
Run these commands from the repository:

uv run openzilo --version
uv run openzilo device use
uv run openzilo info
uv run openzilo device capabilities

--version shows the SDK version. info shows the device model and firmware. device capabilities lists supported features and recording parameter limits.

import asyncio
import openzilo as sdk

ADDRESS = "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"  # Replace with the scanned device address

async def main():
    ring = await sdk.connect_ring(address=ADDRESS)
    try:
        info = await sdk.get_system_info(ring)
        print("Firmware:", info.firmware_version)
        if ring.capabilities.supports("recording_control"):
            print("Recording configuration:", await sdk.get_audio_recording_config(ring))
        else:
            print("No compatible remote recording interface is available")
    finally:
        await ring.disconnect()

asyncio.run(main())

supports() checks that the device and SDK share a compatible feature interface version. See SDK and firmware compatibility.

Firmware versions

items.title: Reading version notes
items.text:
• Supported since firmware XXX identifies the firmware that introduced a feature.
  • Available since SDK XXX identifies the SDK that introduced its API.
  • This page applies to firmware XXX identifies the device behavior described by the page.

Remote recording, recording settings and live audio are available starting with V2.001.0002.0001. The relevant usages state their minimum firmware version. See version migration for other changes from V2.001.0002.0000 to V2.001.0002.0001.

items.text: Read the supported model, hardware revisions and starting versions in official firmware releases, then follow the firmware update guide.

items.title: OpenZilo BLE protocol reference
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Connection requirements

Your computer needs Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE). The SDK communicates with the ring through NUS and supports protocol v4.

items.title: 1. Scope
items.text:
This reference describes protocol v4 framing, commands and fields used by the SDK. Firmware may implement only a subset; query features to check. Button and LED behavior is covered by the user guide.

See the API index for calls and architecture for transport and audio handling.

items.title: 2. BLE services
items.text:
The protocol uses Nordic UART Service (NUS):

Purpose UUID Direction Service 6E400001-B5A3-F393-E0A9-E50E24DCCA9E Service identifier. TX Characteristic 6E400003-B5A3-F393-E0A9-E50E24DCCA9E Ring notifies SDK. RX Characteristic 6E400002-B5A3-F393-E0A9-E50E24DCCA9E SDK writes to ring.

Connect by the scanned address (UUID on macOS), without depending on advertising names.

SDK RX writes use chunks of up to 20 bytes; the last may be shorter. This is a BLE write policy, not a packet boundary or a replacement for system MTU negotiation. TX notifications can use other sizes; reconstruct them with OpenZiloClient or PacketStream.

items.title: 3. Protocol v4 packets
items.text:
The fixed header is 11 bytes:

Offset Field Type Bytes Description 0 magic_number u8 1 Always 0x3F. 1 version u16 2 Currently 4. 3 command u16 2 Command number. 5 body_length u32 4 Body size in bytes. 9 body_crc u16 2 Body CRC16; 0 for an empty body. 11 body bytes variable Command body.

Header and body integers are network byte order (big-endian). Strings and raw bytes are not reordered. CRC covers only the body, using SDK crc16_compute() with initial value 0xFFFF.

A packet can span notifications and a notification can contain multiple packets. Reconstruct using the fixed header and body_length before parsing. OpenZiloClient and PacketStream do this already.

items.title: 4. Commands
items.text: Function Request/event Response SDK API System information 0x0101 0x0102 get_system_info() Feature discovery 0x0105 0x0106 get_device_capabilities() Command error 0x01FF device response None DeviceError Log storage information 0x0301 0x0302 get_log_storage() Log data 0x0303 0x0304 read_log_chunk() Time synchronization Device requests 0x0401 SDK replies 0x0402 enable_time_sync(), send_time_response() Recording count 0x0501 0x0502 get_audio_file_count() Normal recording extraction 0x0503 0x0504 get_audio_file_info() Recording data 0x0506 0x0505 read_audio_frame() End normal extraction 0x0507 0x0508 end_audio_extract() Fast recording extraction 0x0509 0x0504, consecutive 0x0505 download_audio_file(..., quick=True) V2.001.0002.0000 post-save push Consecutive device 0x0505 No initial 0x0504; metadata queried for recovery receive_auto_audio_file() Recording saved Device 0x050A None wait_audio_record_result(), receive_auto_audio_file() Live audio subscription 0x050D 0x050E set_live_audio_subscription() Live audio data Device 0x050F, 0x0510, 0x0511 None receive_live_audio_file() Delete all recordings 0x050B 0x050C clear_audio_files() Start recording 0x0512 0x0513 start_audio_recording() Stop recording 0x0514 0x0515 stop_audio_recording() Recording status 0x0516 0x0517 get_audio_recording_status() Read recording settings 0x0518 0x0519 get_audio_recording_config() Write recording settings 0x051A 0x051B set_audio_recording_config() Start IMU reports 0x0601 0x0602 start_sensor_report() Stop IMU reports 0x0603 0x0604 stop_sensor_report() IMU batches Device 0x0605 None wait_sensor_data() Physical double tap Device 0x0701 None wait_sensor_double_tap_event() Double button press Device 0x0703 None wait_sensor_key_double_press_event() Single button press Device 0x0704 None wait_sensor_key_single_press_event()

items.title: 5. Message bodies
items.text: All u16, i16 and u32 below are big-endian. A nonzero response error_code makes subsequent fields invalid; a response may contain only that error. Some recording failure paths return no response, so timeout alone does not identify the cause.

items.title: 0x0101 Get system information
items.text: Empty body.

items.title: 0x0102 System information response
items.text: Field Type Bytes Description error_code u16 2 Error code. firmware_version_len u16 2 Firmware version string length. firmware_version UTF-8 variable Firmware version string. system_time u32 4 Unix timestamp in seconds. audio_storage_total u32 4 Total recording storage in bytes. audio_storage_available u32 4 Available recording storage in bytes. battery_percent u16 2 Battery percentage. battery_charging u8 1 0 not charging, 1 charging. sn_len u16 2 Serial number string length. sn UTF-8 variable Device serial number. cpuid_len u16 2 CPUID string length. cpuid UTF-8 variable Device CPUID. model_len u16 2 Model string length. model UTF-8 variable Device model.

items.title: 0x0301 Get log storage
items.text: Empty body.

items.title: 0x0302 Log storage response
items.text: Field Type Bytes Description error_code u16 2 Error code. page_size u32 4 Log page size or the device's current paging unit. total_len u32 4 Total log data length.

items.title: 0x0303 Read log data
items.text: Field Type Bytes Description index u32 4 Log index. offset u32 4 Starting offset. size u32 4 Requested byte count.

items.title: 0x0304 Log data response
items.text: Field Type Bytes Description error_code u16 2 Error code. data_len u32 4 Actual data length. data bytes data_len Log bytes.

items.title: 0x0401 Device time request
items.text: Field Type Bytes Description request_time u32 4 Request construction timestamp T1.

items.title: 0x0402 SDK time response
items.text: Field Type Bytes Description request_time u32 4 Original request timestamp T1. response_time u32 4 Request arrival timestamp T2. send_time u32 4 Reply send timestamp T3.

items.title: 0x0501 Get recording count
items.text: Empty body.

items.title: 0x0502 Recording count response
items.text: Field Type Bytes Description error_code u16 2 Error code. file_count u32 4 Number of stored recordings.

items.title: 0x0503 Begin normal extraction
items.text: Field Type Bytes Description error_code u16 2 Always 0. file_index u32 4 Recording file index.

items.title: 0x0509 Begin fast extraction
items.text: Same body as 0x0503. The device first returns 0x0504, then consecutive 0x0505 packets until is_end=1.

items.title: 0x0504 Recording file information
items.text: Field Type Bytes Description error_code u16 2 Error code. file_index u32 4 Recording file index. record_time u32 4 Recording timestamp in seconds. data_size u32 4 Total encoded data bytes.

items.title: 0x0505 Recording data chunk
items.text:
Field Type Bytes Description error_code u16 2 Error code. file_index u32 4 Recording file index. frame_offset u32 4 Byte offset within recording data. frame_size u32 4 Chunk byte count, currently at most 4096. is_end u8 1 0 not final, 1 final chunk. data bytes frame_size Encoded recording bytes.

data is a raw file fragment: OP2C on Opus firmware, or consecutive little-endian two-byte lengths followed by Speex payloads on legacy firmware. See recording formats. File-internal little-endian lengths do not change big-endian protocol fields.

After saving, legacy Speex firmware pushes this same 0x0505 format without preceding 0x0504. receive_auto_audio_file() selects the first frame's index, assembles by offset, and finishes at is_end=1. It returns (file_index, raw_audio) without AudioFileInfo.

Normal continuous push needs no extraction commands. For a gap, timeout or damaged frame, the SDK queries and verifies index and data_size using 0x0503 -> 0x0504, then requests the expected offset with 0x0506, up to three attempts. Results are bounded by data_size. Keep BLE connected during saving and push. If connection was too late, query the recording count and download by index.

items.title: 0x0506 Request recording offset
items.text:
Field Type Bytes Description error_code u16 2 Always 0. file_index u32 4 Recording file index. frame_offset u32 4 Byte offset to read or recover. reserved u16 2 Reserved padding required by current firmware length checks; always 0.

The SDK uses frame_offset for the next normal-download chunk and to recover missing fast-download or push data.

items.title: 0x0507 End normal extraction
items.text: Field Type Bytes Description error_code u16 2 Always 0. file_index u32 4 Recording file index.

items.title: 0x0508 Extraction-end response
items.text: Field Type Bytes Description error_code u16 2 Error code. file_index u32 4 Recording file index.

items.title: 0x050A Recording save result
items.text:
Field Type Bytes Description error_code u16 2 Error code. file_index u32 4 Newly saved recording index.

Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 sends this after saving instead of pushing 0x0505. Retrieve using normal 0x0503 extraction and finish with 0x0507. Failed saves may return only error_code.

items.title: 0x050B Delete all recordings
items.text: Empty body. Irreversibly deletes all recordings on the device.

items.title: 0x050C Delete response
items.text: Field Type Bytes Description error_code u16 2 Error code.

items.title: 0x050D Live audio subscription
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

Field Type Bytes Description enabled u8 1 1 enable, 0 disable.

Subscribing does not start recording; users still hold the button in recording mode. Live-only output uses BLE without flash saving; configurable firmware can also save a copy. Disconnect clears the subscription. Unsubscribe aborts live transmission.

items.title: 0x050E Subscription response
items.text: Field Type Bytes Description error_code u16 2 Error code; notifications disabled or ATT MTU below 128 causes an error. enabled u8 1 Current device subscription state.

items.title: 0x050F Live recording START
items.text: Field Type Bytes Description session_id u32 4 Nonzero recording session ID. reserved u32 4 Always 0. record_time u32 4 Recording timestamp in seconds. reserved u32 4 Always 0. sample_rate u16 2 Always 16000. channels u8 1 1 or 2, matching recording settings. codec u8 1 Always 3 (Opus).

items.title: 0x0510 Live recording DATA
items.text:
Field Type Bytes Description session_id u32 4 Same as 0x050F. sequence u32 4 Packet sequence starting at 0. byte_offset u32 4 Offset in transmitted Opus bytes, starting at 0. length u16 2 Opus packet length, 1–100 bytes. data bytes length One 20 ms Opus packet, with the START channel count.

byte_offset counts Opus data only, excluding OP2C length prefixes.

items.title: 0x0511 Live recording END
items.text:
Field Type Bytes Description error_code u16 2 Error code. session_id u32 4 Same as 0x050F. reserved u32 4 Always 0. produced_bytes u32 4 Opus bytes produced by the device encoder. sent_bytes u32 4 Opus bytes sent by the device. dropped_frames u32 4 Frames dropped by the device.

A recording is complete only when error_code=0, dropped_frames=0, and both byte counts equal the actual received data. Downloads during live recording may receive device-busy in 0x0504.

items.title: 5.5 Live IMU
items.text: Firmware V2.001.0002.0000 requires gesture mode first. Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 removes mode switching and starts capture directly on 0x0601. Both retain the following command numbers.

items.title: 0x0601 Start live reports
items.text:
Empty body. Direct capture startup requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later. Firmware V2.001.0002.0000 requires gesture mode first. Starting from stopped resets sequence_start; an active subscription does not reset it.

Use this sequence:

Firmware V2.001.0002.0001: no mode change required
-> Send 0x0601
-> Receive 0x0602 with error_code=0
-> Receive batch 0x0605

In recording mode on V2.001.0002.0000, 0x0601 returns device-busy. Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 has no such mode restriction. wait_sensor_data() only waits for data and does not send 0x0601.

items.title: 0x0602 Start-report response
items.text: Field Type Bytes Description error_code u16 2 Error code. sample_rate_hz u16 2 Current sample rate; use this returned value. accel_range_g u16 2 Accelerometer range. gyro_range_dps u16 2 Gyroscope range.

items.title: 0x0603 Stop live reports
items.text: Empty body. Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 stops both BLE reporting and IMU capture. Firmware V2.001.0002.0000 only stops BLE reports and can retain local capture in gesture mode.

items.title: 0x0604 Stop-report response
items.text: Field Type Bytes Description error_code u16 2 Error code.

items.title: 0x0605 Single-sample and batch IMU data
items.text:
A successful single-sample body is error_code:u16 + sequence:u32 + timestamp_ms:u32 + accel_x/y/z:i16 + gyro_x/y/z:i16, exactly 22 big-endian bytes. The SDK returns a one-sample SensorDataBatch.

Batch format follows; its successful length is 10 + 16*N, distinct from single-sample format:

Field Type Bytes Description error_code u16 2 Error code. sequence_start u32 4 First sample sequence in this batch. frame_count u16 2 Samples in this batch. sample_size u16 2 Bytes per sample, currently 16. samples bytes frame_count * sample_size Consecutive samples.

Each 16-byte sample has this layout:

Field Type Bytes Description timestamp_ms u32 4 Device capture timestamp in milliseconds. accel_x i16 2 Raw X-axis acceleration. accel_y i16 2 Raw Y-axis acceleration. accel_z i16 2 Raw Z-axis acceleration. gyro_x i16 2 Raw X-axis gyroscope value. gyro_y i16 2 Raw Y-axis gyroscope value. gyro_z i16 2 Raw Z-axis gyroscope value.

Successful body length must equal:

2 + 4 + 2 + 2 + frame_count * sample_size

Batches contain at most 32 samples; use frame_count for the actual size. The next sequence is sequence_start + frame_count. Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 stops capture on disconnect and requires another 0x0601 after reconnecting. Firmware V2.001.0002.0000 can resume local gesture-mode detection after reconnecting, but reporting still needs another subscription.

items.title: 5.6 Motion and button events
items.text: Both V2.001.0002.0000 and V2.001.0002.0001 retain these event layouts. Changes to capture conditions and single-press behavior are described below.

items.title: 0x0701 Physical double tap
items.text:
Field Type Bytes Description timestamp_ms u32 4 Event timestamp in milliseconds.

Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 needs 0x0601 to start IMU capture before detecting taps. Firmware V2.001.0002.0000 detects taps in gesture mode without BLE sample reporting. Timestamps are milliseconds since boot, unlike the device-second timestamps of button events.

items.title: 0x0703 Double button press
items.text:
Field Type Bytes Description timestamp_ms u32 4 Device timestamp in seconds; SDK retains the field name timestamp_ms.

A recognized double press emits only 0x0703, without the corresponding single press or mode change.

items.title: 0x0704 Single button press
items.text:
Field Type Bytes Description timestamp_ms u32 4 Device timestamp in seconds; SDK retains the field name timestamp_ms.

Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 only emits 0x0704, without switching modes. Firmware V2.001.0002.0000 also attempts to switch recording/gesture modes. Confirmation waits for the double-press window; the body has no mode field.

After synchronization, button seconds represent device Unix time. Before synchronization, do not interpret them as calendar time. Do not compare directly with IMU/tap milliseconds since boot.

items.title: 5.7 Remote recording and settings
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

These commands implement recording-control interface v1. Start, status and configuration-read requests have empty bodies. Integers are big-endian. See recording control for application examples.

items.title: 0x0512 / 0x0513 Start recording
items.text: Empty request. A successful response is error_code:u16, session_id:u32, six bytes. Nonzero session ID confirms acceptance, not completion; query 0x0516 for final status. After START timeout, query status instead of automatically retrying.

items.title: 0x0514 / 0x0515 Stop recording
items.text: Request: session_id:u32, cancel:u8. cancel=0 stops according to output settings; cancel=1 discards uncommitted audio. Success: error_code:u16, session_id:u32. The ID must match; final status must still be awaited.

items.title: 0x0516 / 0x0517 Query recording status
items.text:
Empty request. Successful response is 14 bytes:

Field Type Description error_code u16 Error code for the status query. session_id u32 Session ID; 0 when idle. state u8 0 idle, 1 queued, 2 capturing, 3 finalizing, 4 complete, 5 failed, 6 cancelled. saved u8 1 if a device file was saved, otherwise 0. recording_error u16 Recording error code, separate from the query error. file_index u32 Saved file index; 0 if not saved.

The SDK uses saved to determine whether the index is valid. Without a saved file, returned file_index is None.

items.title: 0x0518 / 0x0519 Read recording configuration
items.text:
Empty request. Response begins with error_code:u16; on success the 14-byte settings below are followed by sample rate, frame duration and fixed codec parameters.

Field Type Description version u8 Configuration structure version, currently 1. output u8 0 automatic, 1 flash, 2 live, 3 live plus flash. disconnect_policy u8 0 stop, 1 continue saving on device. channels u8 1 or 2. bitrate u32 Bitrate in bit/s. gain_left_q8, gain_right_q8 u16 each Left/right digital gain; 256 means 1x. max_duration_ms u16 Maximum duration in milliseconds.

Successful responses are 34 bytes. Settings are followed by sample_rate:u16, frame_duration_ms:u16, then codec:u8, complexity:u8, vbr:u8, constrained_vbr:u8, dtx:u8, fec:u8, packet_loss_percent:u8, signal:u16, bit_depth:u8, max_packet_size:u16, application:u16. The device returns these fixed parameters; configuration writes cannot change them.

items.title: 0x051A / 0x051B Write recording configuration
items.text: Request contains only the 14-byte settings above. Response matches configuration readback, showing accepted settings. Write only while idle. Continue-saving on disconnect requires flash or live-plus-flash output.

items.title: 6. Error codes
items.text:
Value Name Description 0 SUCCESS Success. 1 UNKNOWN Unknown error. 2 DEVICE_BUSY Device busy. 3 FILE_NOT_EXIST File not found. 4 CMD_GROUP_NOT_EXIST Command group not found. 5 CMD_NOT_EXIST Command not found. 6 TIMEOUT Operation timed out. 7 PARAM_INVALID Invalid argument. 8 COMMUNICATION Communication error. 9 UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA Unsupported message structure version.

See the firmware update guide. The SDK provides update_firmware() and ota-update; calls are documented in the SDK firmware updates.

items.title: Capability discovery messages
items.text:
The release tags for V2.001.0002.0000 and V2.001.0002.0001 do not implement the discovery commands below. This section documents the SDK parser for the discovery extension; it does not attribute that extension to the V2.001.0002.0001 release.

Protocol v4 and existing GET_INFO and recording-v1 layouts remain unchanged. All integers are big-endian.

Command Direction Body 0x0105 Host → device Empty 0x0106 Device → host error:u16; success adds schema:u8=1 followed by TLVs 0x01FF Device → host original_command:u16, error:u16, exactly four bytes

Errors: 2 busy, 5 unknown command, 7 invalid argument, 9 unsupported structure version. An unknown command returns 5, nonempty discovery request returns 7, and unknown version in the 14-byte recording settings returns 9. Existing command-specific errors remain valid; not all legacy failures use generic errors. Never reply to an error with another error.

TLVs contain tag:u16, length:u16, value:length bytes, within v4's 5120-byte limit; current firmware constructs responses in a buffer of at most 512 bytes. Duplicate tags, truncation, invalid UTF-8 and missing required device fields fail parsing. Unknown optional tags are skipped; an unknown tag with its top bit set requires an SDK upgrade.

Tag Content 1 Full firmware version, UTF-8. 2 Product model, UTF-8. 3 Firmware compilation target, UTF-8. 4 Eight-byte random boot_id for this boot. 5 Firmware build ID, UTF-8. 6 Supported protocol versions as consecutive u16 values; currently 4. 0x0100 + feature_id Feature interface version major:u8, minor:u8. 0x0204 Recording limits, defined below.

Feature IDs: 1 system/1, 2 time_sync/1, 3 audio_files/1, 4 recording_control/1, 5 live_audio/1, 6 imu/2, 7 key_events/1, 8 double_tap/1, 9 ota/1, 10 gesture/1. The suffix is the supported major version. Current firmware does not advertise gesture. IMU/2 starts capture on subscription; an implementation requiring separate gesture mode must not advertise it.

Firmware advertises features only for fully registered command groups. Button/tap events require connected producers in the product build. Advertisement identifies implementation support, not successful hardware initialization, current connection readiness or an idle device.

Recording limits occupy exactly 26 bytes:

Position Type Meaning 1–2 u16, u16 Sample rate and frame duration in milliseconds. 3–6 u8 × 4 Channel mask, output mask, continue-saving output mask, reserved=0. 7–8 u32 × 2 Minimum and maximum bitrate, inclusive. 9–10 u16 × 2 Minimum and maximum Q8 digital gain. 11–13 u16 × 3 Minimum and maximum duration, and duration step in milliseconds.

Masks use enum values as bit positions: channels 1/2 give 0x06; CONTINUE_SAVING with FLASH=1/BOTH=3 gives 0x0A. Recording interface v1 requires these limits. Read fixed Opus parameters through the existing configuration-read command.

items.title: Interface evolution
items.text:
Use optional TLVs for additive fields so older clients can skip them. Incompatible fields or behavior need a higher major version and new command or structure. Mark client-required fields as required. Reject unsupported fields in writes. Detect recording formats from content, independently of current firmware.

Requests have no transaction IDs. Query state before retrying START. Release notes specify OTA compatibility; the SDK does not infer every starting-version combination or provide automatic rollback. Application and bootloader security versions are independent.

items.title: Remote recording and configuration
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Start and stop recordings with Python or the CLI, and configure channels, bitrate, gain and maximum duration. Audio can be saved on the ring, streamed to the computer, or both.

Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later. V2.001.0002.0000 does not provide remote start, stop, status or recording configuration APIs.

items.title: Record with the CLI
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

Select a device, then record five seconds and download it:

uv run openzilo device use
uv run openzilo audio-record recordings/test.wav --seconds 5 --channels 1

WAV output requires ffmpeg. Inspect settings and recording status:

uv run openzilo audio-config
uv run openzilo audio-status

See the CLI guide for all commands.

items.title: Record and save with Python
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

Replace ADDRESS with the scanned address. This example stores five seconds on the ring, waits for saving, and downloads the completed recording:

import asyncio
import openzilo as sdk

ADDRESS = "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"

async def main():
    ring = await sdk.connect_ring(address=ADDRESS)
    try:
        if not ring.capabilities.supports("recording_control"):
            print("No compatible remote recording interface is available")
            return
        config = sdk.AudioRecordingConfig(
            output=sdk.AudioOutput.FLASH,
            channels=1,
            bitrate=16000,
            max_duration_ms=5000,
        )
        await sdk.set_audio_recording_config(ring, config)
        session_id = await sdk.start_audio_recording(ring)
        status = await sdk.wait_audio_recording_finished(ring, session_id)
        if status.saved:
            info, data = await sdk.download_audio_file(ring, status.file_index)
            bundle = sdk.save_audio_bundle(
                file_index=info.file_index, data=data, output_dir="recordings",
            )
            print(bundle.play_path)
    finally:
        await ring.disconnect()

asyncio.run(main())

items.title: Change recording settings
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

Read with get_audio_recording_config() and write with set_audio_recording_config(). Changes are allowed only while idle, survive reconnection and reset on reboot.

Setting Argument Values/range Output output AUTO automatic, FLASH save on device, LIVE stream, LIVE_AND_FLASH stream and save Channels channels 1 or 2 Bitrate bitrate 8000–32000 bit/s Digital gain gain_left_q8, gain_right_q8 0–1024; 256 means 1x Maximum duration max_duration_ms 20–60000 ms in multiples of 20 Disconnect handling disconnect_policy STOP or CONTINUE_SAVING on device

Sample rate is fixed at 16 kHz with 20 ms frames. The device also reports allowed ranges, checked by the SDK before writing. Other fixed Opus parameters can be read but not changed through this API.

CONTINUE_SAVING requires FLASH or LIVE_AND_FLASH.

items.title: Stop early or cancel
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

start_audio_recording() returns the recording session_id, not completion. To stop early:

await sdk.stop_audio_recording(ring, session_id)
status = await sdk.wait_audio_recording_finished(ring, session_id)

Pass cancel=True to discard an uncommitted recording. A stop response does not establish that a file was saved; query or wait for completion.

If START times out, query get_audio_recording_status() instead of repeating START. Session IDs last only for the current device boot and cannot be reused after reboot.

items.title: Stream with a device copy
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

For LIVE or LIVE_AND_FLASH, subscribe before starting. Call start_audio_recording() from receive_live_audio_file()'s on_subscribed callback. See remote_recording.py.

Interrupted live audio cannot resume across connections. With simultaneous saving, the device copy can be downloaded after saving finishes. Live-only disconnect fails that transfer.

items.title: API quick reference
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

API Result get_audio_recording_config(ring) Current AudioRecordingConfig. set_audio_recording_config(ring, config) Configuration read back from the device. start_audio_recording(ring) Recording session_id. stop_audio_recording(ring, session_id, cancel=False) Session ID confirmed by the device. get_audio_recording_status(ring) AudioRecordingStatus, including state, saved flag, file index and error. wait_audio_recording_finished(ring, session_id, timeout_s=75.0, poll_interval_s=0.2) Final status; raises for a failed recording.

All APIs above are asynchronous. Except the completion waiter, they accept timeout_s for a single request timeout.
