items.title: Ring user guide
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Firmware versions

This guide covers device operation in V2.001.0002.0000 and V2.001.0002.0001. V2.001.0002.0001 removes recording/gesture mode switching; the relevant sections identify the changes.

items.title: Start here
items.text:
• First use: charge, connect, record and download audio.
  • Buttons and modes: recording, mode changes and button events.
  • LED indicators: colors and patterns, with suggested actions.
  • Firmware updates: package selection, updates and recovery.

items.title: Build an application
items.text:
Use the CLI guide to operate the device, or the Python SDK guide to write an application. Check feature requirements before choosing an API.

Hardware, firmware and SDK versions are managed separately. Use the interfaces supported by your device. The Python SDK does not currently expose PPG data APIs.

items.title: Get help
items.text: When reporting an issue, include SDK and firmware versions, steps to reproduce, and error messages. Remove device addresses, serial numbers and private audio. Report security issues privately as described in the security policy.

items.title: Buttons and Modes
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Firmware versions

This guide covers device operation in V2.001.0002.0000 and V2.001.0002.0001. V2.001.0002.0001 removes recording/gesture mode switching; the relevant sections identify the changes.

Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 removes recording/gesture mode switching. The table describes that version; differences for V2.001.0002.0000 follow it.

Action Behavior in V2.001.0002.0001 Single short press Report a single-press event without changing modes. Double button press Report a double-press event without the corresponding single press. Press and hold Start local recording after about 0.3 seconds; release to finish. Physical double tap Report a tap when the application has subscribed to IMU and capture is active.

Firmware V2.001.0002.0000 starts in recording mode and uses a single press to switch recording/gesture modes. Gesture mode does not start button recording and can retain local IMU tap detection. This procedure does not apply to V2.001.0002.0001.

A short press is under about 0.2 seconds. Two presses within roughly 0.5 seconds form a double press, so single-press confirmation has a short delay.

items.title: Recording
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

Live audio, remote recording and recording settings are available starting with V2.001.0002.0001. Choose device storage, live-only output or both. Live-only output leaves no device copy; select simultaneous saving and the continue-saving policy before recording if a device copy must survive disconnection.

Button recordings in V2.001.0002.0000 use Speex and can be pushed after saving. Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 saves Opus (OP2C), notifies with 0x050A, then allows download. The SDK's receive_auto_audio_file() handles both workflows.

Hold the button, speak after the green light appears, then release it. Recording is rejected below 20% reported battery. Local recordings can be saved without BLE. Back up before clearing full storage; downloading does not delete files.

items.title: IMU and Tap Detection
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 needs no mode change. start_sensor_report() starts IMU; stop_sensor_report() or disconnection stops it. Subscribe again after reconnecting. Tap detection starts and stops with capture.

Firmware V2.001.0002.0000 requires gesture mode first and can keep local tap detection after BLE reports stop. Physical double taps (0x0701) differ from double button presses (0x0703).

items.title: Firmware updates
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Update requirements

Use the official OTA package specified in the release notes. Match the device model, hardware revision and starting firmware version. The SDK updates application firmware only, not the bootloader.

items.title: 1. Select a package
items.text:
Open official firmware releases. Confirm that your model and hardware revision are supported, your current version is an allowed starting version, and you have read the data-retention policy and known issues.

Download the versioned signed OTA ZIP and obtain its signing public key independently through a trusted channel. The signed metadata carries the target version, model, board and payload digest. Factory flashing files are not SDK OTA packages.

items.title: 2. Prepare
items.text:
Back up important recordings. Stop recording, downloads and IMU reporting, and disconnect other apps. Ensure sufficient charge according to the release instructions.

From the SDK repository:

uv sync --locked
uv run openzilo device use
uv run openzilo info

Record the current firmware version. Run uv run openzilo ota-update --help to inspect the installed updater.

items.title: 3. Run the update
items.text:
Replace each placeholder with the values for this release:

uv run openzilo ota-inspect "path/to/firmware.ota.zip" --public-key "path/to/trusted-signing-public.pem"
uv run openzilo ota-update "path/to/firmware.ota.zip" --public-key "path/to/trusted-signing-public.pem"

The command uses your saved device; --address selects another one. Keep the ring nearby and avoid interrupting power or Bluetooth.

ota-inspect verifies signatures and displays all metadata offline; add --json for JSON. ota-update checks device model, board and source version before sending only the inner OTA bytes. Raw BIN input and manual version, digest or model overrides are no longer accepted. Test-profile ZIPs require --allow-test-firmware; boards must be reported by the device or provided by an exact verified legacy profile; unknown boards are rejected.

items.title: 4. Confirm completion
items.text:
After transfer, the SDK waits for reboot, reconnects, checks that it is the same device, and reads its firmware version. The command reports success only after the target version is confirmed. Continue waiting when transfer reaches 100%.

Run uv run openzilo info again, record a short clip and check the features your application uses.

Timeouts are in seconds: --timeout defaults to 30 per operation, --total-timeout to 600 for preparation and transfer, and --reboot-timeout to 90 for reboot, reconnect and version checks. See the SDK guide and update_firmware.py for Python integration.

items.title: If the update is interrupted
items.text:
Reconnect and read the firmware version before retrying after a timeout, disconnect or cancellation. Exiting the computer-side updater does not withdraw a package already received by the ring.

If reconnection fails, record the starting version, target version and error message, then contact support. Downgrade, recovery and recording retention depend on the release instructions.

items.title: First use
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Firmware versions

This guide covers device operation in V2.001.0002.0000 and V2.001.0002.0001. V2.001.0002.0001 removes recording/gesture mode switching; the relevant sections identify the changes.

items.title: 1. Charge the ring
items.text: Use the supplied charging accessory. Red flashes indicate charging; steady green indicates a full charge. Charge before recording, especially when the device reports less than 20% battery. See LED indicators.

items.title: 2. Install and connect
items.text:
You need Python 3.10 or later, uv, and Bluetooth Low Energy support. Linux also requires BlueZ and permission to access Bluetooth. Install ffmpeg to convert recordings to WAV.

git clone https://github.com/ziloai/OpenZilo.git
cd OpenZilo
uv sync --locked
uv run openzilo device use
uv run openzilo info

Select a ring from the scan results. Its address is saved locally. Close other apps connected to the ring first. info shows the model, firmware version and battery level.

Later commands use the saved device. Run device use again to change it, or supply --address for an individual command.

items.title: 3. Record and download audio
items.text:
Hold the button, speak after the green light appears, then release to finish. Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 needs no recording-mode change. If V2.001.0002.0000 is in gesture mode, return to recording mode using Buttons and modes.

uv run openzilo audio-count
uv run openzilo audio-download 0 first-recording.wav

Confirm the count increased, then download file index 0. This is the first stored recording, not necessarily the latest one. The command produces a playable WAV and preserves the original data.

If conversion fails, check that ffmpeg -version runs. Keep the original .bin file for conversion later. Renaming its extension does not convert the audio.

items.title: 4. Receive IMU data
items.text:
Direct startup requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later. On V2.001.0002.0000, enter gesture mode with a short press first, then run:

uv run openzilo sensor-stream --seconds 10

Move your hand to see data in the terminal. The command stops reporting and disconnects when finished; Ctrl+C ends it early. Check feature requirements for other firmware.

items.title: Next steps
items.text:
Use the interactive CLI for repeated operations, or the Python SDK to build an app. See Recording control to start recordings remotely and change recording settings.

For connection issues, check battery, Bluetooth permissions and other connected apps. For recording issues, check mode, battery and storage. For IMU issues, check mode and the start-report response. More help is in the SDK FAQ.

items.title: LED Indicators
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Firmware versions

This guide covers device operation in V2.001.0002.0000 and V2.001.0002.0001. V2.001.0002.0001 removes recording/gesture mode switching; the relevant sections identify the changes.

The same color can mean different things. Use the action you just performed and the blink pattern together.

When Indicator Meaning / next step Startup / reset White for about 0.2 seconds The ring has started. This does not confirm a Bluetooth connection. Charging Red, about 0.5 seconds on / 0.5 seconds off Charging is in progress. Fully charged Steady green while the charging status remains full Charging is complete. Recording Steady green Audio recording is active. Release the button to finish. V2.001.0002.0000 successful mode switch Blue twice, about 0.5 seconds on / 0.5 seconds off The recording / gesture mode changed. Both directions use the same indication. Recording transfer Blue, about 0.5 seconds on / 0.5 seconds off A recording transfer is active. Recording or IMU-start error Three quick red pulses, about 0.1 seconds on / off The operation failed. Check battery, available storage, and the current mode. Low-battery indication Red for about 2 seconds, then off Charge the ring. A short press can request this indication when the battery is low. Critical-battery indication Brief red for about 0.3 seconds, then off Charge the ring before continuing. The indication alone does not confirm power-off.

The low-battery and critical-battery indications are continuous red intervals, not three flashes. Startup, mode changes, and error indications are brief and can be missed.

Indicators can interrupt one another: battery warnings take precedence over mode changes, recording / transfer, and charging. Recording and a full charge both use green, so the LED alone cannot identify the state. Recording / transfer completion ends the corresponding indication; another active indication, such as charging, may then appear.

See Buttons and Modes and First Use.

Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 removes recording/gesture mode switching; do not use that blue indication to infer a mode.

items.title: Signed firmware bundles
items.text:
• Add inspect_firmware_bundle() and ota-inspect for offline signature verification and complete metadata display, including JSON output.
  • Verify the manifest signature, signing key ID, payload digest, length and encrypted APP header before an update starts.
  • Check device model, board and allowed starting versions before transmitting only the inner OTA payload. Reconnect and verify the full running version after reboot.
  • Require explicit opt-in for test-profile bundles. Verification requires an independently trusted P-256 public key; a downloaded bundle cannot supply its own trust anchor.

items.title: Local IMU calibration
items.text:
• Add six-face accelerometer fitting, stationary gyroscope bias fitting and independent validation.
  • Store validated profiles locally, bound to the device identifier, model, exact firmware version and sensor ranges.
  • Add imu-calibrate and explicit calibrated streams in g and deg/s. Preserve raw streaming and avoid applying corrections twice.
  • Perform all calibration on the host without writing calibration parameters to the ring. A new firmware image is not required for supported IMU contracts.

items.title: Breaking change and migration
items.text:
update_firmware() and ota-update now accept only signed OTA ZIPs. Raw BIN input and the version, sha256 and expected_model overrides have been removed. Version and compatibility fields come from verified metadata.

from pathlib import Path
import openzilo as sdk

# ring is an already connected OpenZiloClient.
bundle = Path("firmware.ota.zip").read_bytes()
public_key = Path("trusted-signing-public.pem").read_bytes()
metadata = sdk.inspect_firmware_bundle(bundle, trusted_public_key=public_key)
info = await sdk.update_firmware(ring, bundle, trusted_public_key=public_key)

cryptography>=43 is now a required dependency. Existing firmware OTA wire protocols remain unchanged. Device-side encryption-key matching and rollback enforcement remain device checks; host verification does not confirm installation or hardware calibration accuracy.

items.title: Decode and save audio
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Detect Speex or Opus recordings, preserve the original file and convert to playable audio. These functions process local bytes without an active BLE connection. See live audio for the PyAV dependency used by live PCM.

Code snippets use import openzilo as sdk; ring is a connected client. See the quick start for a complete connection example.

items.title: Audio decoding
items.text:
A recording .bin contains legacy Speex frames or mono/stereo Opus in OP2C format. The SDK preserves it, detects its encoding from the content, and uses ffmpeg to produce WAV. See recording formats.

bundle = sdk.save_audio_bundle(file_index=0, data=raw_audio, output_dir="audio")
print(bundle.raw_path)
print(bundle.play_path)

Without ffmpeg, downloading still works, but decoding raises SpeexDecoderUnavailable or OpusDecoderUnavailable.

items.title: save_audio_bundle()
items.text:
Purpose: preserve raw recording data and attempt playable WAV output.

bundle = sdk.save_audio_bundle(
    file_index=0,
    data=raw_audio,
    metadata={"record_time": info.record_time},
    output_dir="audio",
)
print(bundle.raw_path)
print(bundle.play_path)

Returns: AudioBundle.

Missing ffmpeg or decoding failure raises SpeexDecoderUnavailable, OpusDecoderUnavailable or AudioDecodeError.

items.title: Audio decoding helpers
items.text:
• decode_audio_to_wav(): return WAV bytes for application-managed storage.
  • build_playable_audio(): return PlayableAudio with bytes, extension, MIME and decoding description.
  • decode_speex_to_pcm(), decode_opus_to_pcm(): return decoded PCM for further processing.
  • parse_opus_recording(), build_opus_recording(): read and write OP2C files.
  • build_wav_from_pcm(): wrap PCM in a WAV header.
  • decode_ogg_speex_with_ffmpeg(): low-level ffmpeg invocation.
  • parse_packetized_speex_stream(), split_raw_speex_packets(), build_ogg_speex(): Speex packet utilities.
  • normalize_decoded_speex_pcm(): correct decoded PCM length.
  • normalize_pcm_config(), format_pcm_config(): normalize and display PCM configuration.
  • build_audio_bundle_paths(), build_base_name(): generate output paths and base filenames.
  • is_wav(), is_ogg_speex(): detect formats.
  • pick_speex_mode(), pick_frame_size(), pick_bits_size(): derive Speex parameters.

Low-level parse_packetized_speex_stream() also accepts legacy 1026-byte outer blocks. High-level decode_speex_to_pcm(), build_playable_audio(), decode_audio_to_wav() and save_audio_bundle() default to allow_framed_blocks=False. Pass True explicitly for that legacy input.

items.title: Scan and connect
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Scan for nearby devices and manage the BLE connection. Start with the quick start; see compatibility for feature discovery after connecting.

Code snippets use import openzilo as sdk; ring is a connected client. See the quick start for a complete connection example.

items.title: scan_rings()
items.text:
Purpose: scan nearby BLE devices, optionally filtering by address.

Signature:

devices = await scan_rings(address=None, timeout_s=25.0)

Returns: list[BleDeviceInfo].

timeout_s limits the scan duration and defaults to 25 seconds. Supply another positive value if needed.

Common exception: TransportError if bleak is missing.

Example:

devices = await sdk.scan_rings(address="AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF")
print(devices)

items.title: connect_ring()
items.text:
Purpose: create and connect an OpenZiloClient.

Signature:

ring = await connect_ring(
    address="AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF",
    command_timeout_s=10.0,
    auto_time_sync=False,
    negotiate_capabilities=True,
    allow_unverified_features=False,
)

Returns: a connected OpenZiloClient.

Features are discovered automatically. Call await ring.disconnect() in finally. With async with OpenZiloClient(...), discover features explicitly through get_device_capabilities().

items.title: OpenZiloClient
items.text:
Purpose: manage BLE connection, packet reception, requests and event waits.

Typical usage:

async with sdk.OpenZiloClient(address=ADDRESS) as ring:
    packet = await ring.request(0x0101, 0x0102)

Common members:

  • is_connected: whether the connection is currently open.
  • connect() / disconnect(): connect and disconnect manually.
  • send_command(command, body=b""): send without waiting for a response.
  • request(command, response_command, body=b"", timeout_s=None): send and await the specified response.
  • wait_for_command(command, timeout_s=None): await an event or subsequent response.
  • add_packet_handler(command, handler, queue_packets=True): register a synchronous or asynchronous handler. With False, the handler exclusively receives this command and no queue copy is retained; do not mix with other handlers or waiters for that command. Exceptions are logged to openzilo without affecting other packets. Disconnect cancels unfinished asynchronous handlers.
  • remove_packet_handler(command, handler): remove a handler.

Each command queue holds at most 256 packets by default; configure OpenZiloClient(receive_queue_size=...) to change it. Overflow clears the backlog and reports ProtocolError through waiting APIs instead of treating lost data as success. For callback-only use, prefer queue_packets=False. Handlers should return promptly; manage concurrency within asynchronous handlers.

Requests expecting the same response command are serialized. Recording download, automatic reception, frame reads and deletion cannot compete on one connection; conflicts immediately raise ProtocolError. Applications combining low-level recording functions must manage the whole session. OTA rejects ordinary commands from other tasks, except automatic time replies. Stop recording and IMU before OTA.

Failed or cancelled normal downloads attempt an end command with up to two seconds for cleanup. Cleanup failure does not replace the original exception. Without transaction IDs, late responses after a timeout cannot be reliably matched; reconnect before retrying when strict isolation is required.

items.title: FirmwareBundle
items.text: The immutable result of inspect_firmware_bundle() contains version, model, board, profile, security_version, source_versions, signing_key_id, and inner OTA bytes payload. Its manifest property returns a fresh dictionary of every verified field, suitable for display or JSON output. Mutating that copy cannot change update data. Inspection does not check device compatibility.

items.title: Read device information
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Read the model, firmware, battery and storage information. Feature discovery is not required. Returned fields are listed in data types.

Code snippets use import openzilo as sdk; ring is a connected client. See the quick start for a complete connection example.

items.title: Read device information
items.text:
connect -> get_system_info -> disconnect

async with sdk.OpenZiloClient(address=ADDRESS) as ring:
    info = await sdk.get_system_info(ring)

items.title: get_system_info() and parse_system_info()
items.text:
get_system_info() reads device information. parse_system_info() parses only the 0x0102 body, normally for testing.

info = await sdk.get_system_info(ring)
print(info.firmware_version, info.battery_percent)

Returns: SystemInfo.

Common exceptions: TimeoutError for timeout, DeviceError for a device error code.

items.title: Download and receive saved recordings
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Download recordings already stored on the device, or receive a recording after it finishes saving. See live audio for streaming and remote recording for configuration and control.

Code snippets use import openzilo as sdk; ring is a connected client. See the quick start for a complete connection example.

items.title: Download and save a recording
items.text:
connect -> get_audio_file_count -> download_audio_file -> save_audio_bundle

async with sdk.OpenZiloClient(address=ADDRESS) as ring:
    count = await sdk.get_audio_file_count(ring)
    if count:
        info, raw_audio = await sdk.download_audio_file(ring, file_index=0)
        bundle = sdk.save_audio_bundle(
            file_index=info.file_index,
            data=raw_audio,
            metadata={"record_time": info.record_time},
            output_dir="audio",
        )
        print(bundle.raw_path)
        print(bundle.play_path)

download_audio_file() defaults to fast download (quick=True). With quick=False, the SDK requests each data chunk separately.

items.title: Receive a recording after it finishes
items.text:
connect -> wait in receive_auto_audio_file -> hold the button to record, then release
        -> download after 0x050A on firmware `V2.001.0002.0001` / receive 0x0505 on legacy firmware -> save_audio_bundle

async with sdk.OpenZiloClient(address=ADDRESS) as ring:
    print("Hold the ring button to record, then release")
    file_index, raw_audio = await sdk.receive_auto_audio_file(
        ring,
        timeout_s=60.0,
    )
    bundle = sdk.save_audio_bundle(
        file_index=file_index,
        data=raw_audio,
        output_dir="audio",
    )
    print(bundle.raw_path)
    print(bundle.play_path)

Automatic transfers from V2.001.0002.0000 do not begin with 0x0504, so the return value has no AudioFileInfo. During normal continuous reception the SDK sends no extra commands. Recovery queries file metadata, verifies the index, and bounds the result by data_size. Keep BLE connected and do not simultaneously call download_audio_file() or read_audio_frame() on the same 0x0505 queue. If you connected too late, query the file count and download by index.

items.title: Recording transfer sequences
items.text:
The SDK supports normal and fast downloads, plus automatic reception and live streaming:

Transfer Protocol sequence SDK call Fast download 0x0509 -> 0x0504 -> 0x0505...; 0x0506 recovers missing data download_audio_file(..., quick=True) Normal download 0x0503 -> 0x0504, repeated 0x0506 -> 0x0505, then 0x0507 -> 0x0508 download_audio_file(..., quick=False) V2.001.0002.0000 post-save push Consecutive 0x0505... after saving; recovery queries 0x0504 metadata and requests 0x0506 receive_auto_audio_file() V2.001.0002.0001 post-save notification Normal download after 0x050A receive_auto_audio_file() Live recording Subscribe with 0x050D -> 0x050E, then 0x050F -> 0x0510... -> 0x0511 receive_live_audio_file()

Low-level normal-download functions get_audio_file_info(), read_audio_frame() and end_audio_extract() are mainly for debugging.

items.title: download_audio_file()
items.text:
Purpose: download a complete recording by index.

Signature:

info, raw_audio = await download_audio_file(
    client,
    file_index,
    progress=None,
    timeout_s=None,
    quick=True,
)

Returns: tuple[AudioFileInfo, bytes].

Example:

info, raw_audio = await sdk.download_audio_file(
    ring,
    file_index=0,
    progress=sdk.ProgressPrinter(prefix="audio"),
)

file_index starts at 0. Query get_audio_file_count() first to avoid requesting a missing recording.

items.title: receive_auto_audio_file()
items.text:
Purpose: obtain a complete recording immediately after saving. On 0x050A, the SDK performs a normal download and sends 0x0507 to release the file. Legacy firmware instead pushes 0x0505, with metadata queried only for recovery. Both return the original file for automatic encoding detection by save_audio_bundle().

Signature:

file_index, raw_audio = await sdk.receive_auto_audio_file(
    ring,
    timeout_s=60.0,
)

Arguments:

  • client: connected OpenZiloClient, named ring in the examples.
  • timeout_s: maximum seconds for each data arrival; None uses client command_timeout_s.

Returns: tuple[int, bytes].

  • The first value is the file index from 0x050A or the first valid 0x0505.
  • The second is raw audio reconstructed by frame_offset, ready for save_audio_bundle().
  • Legacy push has no initial 0x0504, so no AudioFileInfo is returned. Recovery metadata is used only for integrity and length checks.

Reception behavior:

  • The first frame selects the file index; frames belonging to other files are excluded.
  • Duplicate and overlapping bytes are removed by offset.
  • For gaps, post-first-frame timeouts or damaged frames, the SDK queries and validates file index and exact data_size, then requests the expected offset with 0x0506, up to three retries.
  • Normal reception returns at is_end=True. Recovered data is truncated to data_size without extra bytes.

Exceptions:

  • No initial frame before timeout: TimeoutError.
  • A gap unrecovered after three retries, mismatched metadata index, or invalid frame fields: ProtocolError.
  • Nonzero device error: DeviceError.
  • Disconnected before the call or during the wait: TransportError.

Do not run concurrently with download_audio_file(), read_audio_frame() or other direct 0x0505 waiters. They share a receive queue and can take each other's packets. If connection began too late for the push, use get_audio_file_count() and download_audio_file().

Saving example:

file_index, raw_audio = await sdk.receive_auto_audio_file(ring, timeout_s=60.0)
bundle = sdk.save_audio_bundle(
    file_index=file_index,
    data=raw_audio,
    output_dir="audio",
)

items.title: clear_audio_files()
items.text:
Purpose: delete every recording on the device.

await sdk.clear_audio_files(ring)

This is irreversible. Applications should require explicit confirmation or an environment-specific safeguard.

items.title: Read information, download the first recording, and save it
items.text:
import asyncio
import openzilo as sdk

ADDRESS = "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"


async def main() -> None:
    async with sdk.OpenZiloClient(address=ADDRESS) as ring:
        sdk.enable_time_sync(ring)

        info = await sdk.get_system_info(ring)
        print("system:", info)

        count = await sdk.get_audio_file_count(ring)
        print("audio count:", count)
        if count == 0:
            return

        audio_info, raw_audio = await sdk.download_audio_file(
            ring,
            file_index=0,
            progress=sdk.ProgressPrinter(prefix="audio"),
        )

    bundle = sdk.save_audio_bundle(
        file_index=audio_info.file_index,
        data=raw_audio,
        metadata={"record_time": audio_info.record_time},
        output_dir="audio",
    )
    print("raw:", bundle.raw_path)
    print("play:", bundle.play_path)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

items.title: Exceptions and troubleshooting
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Identify the failure from its exception, then check the connection, device state and call order.

items.title: Exceptions
items.text:
OpenZiloError
# SDK base exception; catch this to handle all SDK failures together.

TransportError
# BLE transport failure: missing bleak, device not found, connection failure, writes while disconnected, or disconnect while waiting.

ProtocolError
# Invalid protocol header, CRC, length or response body.

TimeoutError
# Request queue, write, response or unsolicited-event timeout. Reconnect if a write was interrupted.

DeviceError
error_code: int  # Nonzero device error code.
# Explicit device error, such as busy, invalid argument or missing file.

AudioDecodeError
# Audio cannot be decoded to playable WAV, or ffmpeg exceeds 30 seconds.

SpeexDecoderUnavailable
# ffmpeg is missing or a custom Speex decoder is unavailable.

OpusDecoderUnavailable
# ffmpeg is missing, preventing OP2C decoding.

items.title: TransportError: Install bleak to use BLE transport
items.text:
The current Python environment lacks SDK dependencies, often because the script used a different Python environment. In your project, install the SDK from GitHub:

uv add git+https://github.com/ziloai/OpenZilo.git
uv run python your_script.py

items.title: Cannot discover or connect to a device
items.text:
• Use the scanned address, or UUID on macOS; the SDK does not filter by advertising name.
  • Ensure the ring is advertising and no other application holds its connection.
  • On Windows, try toggling Bluetooth.
  • In PyCharm, ensure the interpreter uses the environment containing the dependencies.

items.title: Timed out waiting for command ...
items.text:
The requested response or event did not arrive before timeout. Common causes:

  • Busy device: recording, writing flash or transferring a large file.
  • Concurrent commands take responses expected by other tasks.
  • Gesture mode was not entered on V2.001.0002.0000, or IMU capture was not started on V2.001.0002.0001.

Prefer one request/response operation at a time on each connection.

items.title: receive_auto_audio_file() times out
items.text:
An initial timeout means no post-save 0x050A or pushed 0x0505 arrived in time. Keep BLE connected and start waiting before asking the user to hold and release the recording button. If connection began too late, query the count and download by index.

Do not run receive_auto_audio_file() with download_audio_file(), read_audio_frame() or direct wait_for_command(0x0505) calls. Shared queue access can cause timeouts or missing offsets.

items.title: start_sensor_report() reports device busy
items.text: Finish conflicting operations. Enter gesture mode with the button on V2.001.0002.0000; call start_sensor_report() directly on V2.001.0002.0001. Wait for a successful response before receiving data.

items.title: Download succeeds but decoding fails
items.text: Check that ffmpeg -version runs. To keep raw audio only, preserve the returned bytes or the raw file written by save_audio_bundle().

items.title: Can deleted recordings be recovered?
items.text: clear_audio_files() deletes all stored recordings, with no SDK recovery. Put it behind an explicit maintenance or test action, never in ordinary startup code.

items.title: Button and tap events
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Wait for device button and tap events. In firmware V2.001.0002.0001, a single press reports an event without switching recording/gesture modes.

Code snippets use import openzilo as sdk; ring is a connected client. See the quick start for a complete connection example.

items.title: Motion and button events
items.text:
0x0701: physical double tap:

With firmware V2.001.0002.0001, start IMU with start_sensor_report() before waiting for taps; detection stops when capture stops. Firmware V2.001.0002.0000 detects taps in gesture mode without BLE sample reporting.

await sdk.start_sensor_report(ring)
try:
    event = await sdk.wait_sensor_double_tap_event(ring, timeout_s=30.0)
    print(event.timestamp_ms)
finally:
    await sdk.stop_sensor_report(ring)

0x0703: double button press:

A recognized double press emits only 0x0703, without a corresponding 0x0704 or mode change.

event = await sdk.wait_sensor_key_double_press_event(ring, timeout_s=30.0)
print(event.timestamp_ms)

0x0704: single button press:

event = await sdk.wait_sensor_key_single_press_event(ring, timeout_s=30.0)
print(event.timestamp_ms)

Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 emits 0x0704 without switching modes. Firmware V2.001.0002.0000 attempts to switch recording/gesture modes and emits the event. Confirmation still waits for the double-press window, and the event body contains no mode field.

items.title: wait_sensor_key_single_press_event()
items.text:
event = await sdk.wait_sensor_key_single_press_event(
    ring,
    timeout_s=30.0,
)
  • Purpose: await the device's unsolicited 0x0704 single-button event.
  • ring: connected OpenZiloClient.
  • timeout_s: maximum wait in seconds; None uses client command_timeout_s.
  • Returns SensorKeySinglePressEvent; timestamp_ms carries device time in seconds on this firmware, retaining a historical field name.
  • Exceptions: SDK TimeoutError on timeout; ProtocolError for damaged packets.

items.title: parse_sensor_key_single_press_event()
items.text:
event = sdk.parse_sensor_key_single_press_event(body)
  • Purpose: parse a 0x0704 body without its 11-byte protocol header, usually for protocol tests or custom reception.
  • body: exactly one network-order u32 timestamp, four bytes.
  • Returns SensorKeySinglePressEvent.
  • Raises ProtocolError for fewer or more than four bytes.

items.title: Collect IMU data
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Start accelerometer and gyroscope reports, receive single-sample or batch data, and stop reporting when finished. Discover device features first. See event handling for button and tap events.

Code snippets use import openzilo as sdk; ring is a connected client. See the quick start for a complete connection example.

items.title: Receive IMU batches
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

connect -> discover features
        -> start_sensor_report succeeds (0x0601 -> 0x0602 error_code=0)
        -> wait_sensor_data loop (receive 0x0605)
        -> stop_sensor_report

Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 starts capture on subscription without a button-based mode change. Firmware V2.001.0002.0000 requires gesture mode first.

async with sdk.OpenZiloClient(address=ADDRESS) as ring:
    await sdk.get_device_capabilities(ring)
    start = await sdk.start_sensor_report(ring)
    print(start)
    try:
        for _ in range(10):
            batch = await sdk.wait_sensor_data(ring, timeout_s=5.0)
            for sample in batch.samples:
                print(batch.sequence_start, sample.timestamp_ms, sample.accel_x)
    finally:
        await sdk.stop_sensor_report(ring)

Start the wait_sensor_data() loop only after start_sensor_report() succeeds. Waiting receives the next 0x0605; it does not send 0x0601 or start the local IMU.

items.title: IMU data
items.text:
Firmware version

Starting capture directly with start_sensor_report() without switching modes requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later. V2.001.0002.0000 requires entering gesture mode with the button first.

Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 removes recording/gesture modes. A BLE connection alone does not start IMU capture:

  • start_sensor_report() (0x0601) starts capture and 0x0605 reporting. Wait for successful 0x0602 before receiving data.
  • stop_sensor_report() (0x0603) stops reports and capture; tap detection stops with capture.
  • Disconnection stops capture; subscribe again after reconnecting.
  • Use the returned SensorStartInfo.sample_rate_hz.

Firmware V2.001.0002.0000 requires gesture mode first and can retain local tap detection after BLE reporting stops. That old procedure does not apply to V2.001.0002.0001.

Current 0x0605 batch body:

error_code: u16
sequence_start: u32
frame_count: u16
sample_size: u16
samples: frame_count * sample_size

Each sample is currently 16 bytes:

timestamp_ms: u32
accel_x: i16
accel_y: i16
accel_z: i16
gyro_x: i16
gyro_y: i16
gyro_z: i16

Usage:

# Firmware V2.001.0002.0001: subscription starts capture without a mode change.
start = await sdk.start_sensor_report(ring)  # Await success before expecting 0x0605
print(start.sample_rate_hz)
try:
    batch = await sdk.wait_sensor_data(ring, timeout_s=5.0)
    for index, sample in enumerate(batch.samples):
        sequence = batch.sequence_start + index
        print(sequence, sample.timestamp_ms, sample.accel_x, sample.gyro_x)
finally:
    await sdk.stop_sensor_report(ring)

items.title: Receive ten IMU batches
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

Firmware V2.001.0002.0001 starts IMU directly; firmware V2.001.0002.0000 requires entering gesture mode using the button first.

import asyncio
import openzilo as sdk

ADDRESS = "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"


async def main() -> None:
    async with sdk.OpenZiloClient(address=ADDRESS) as ring:
        await sdk.get_device_capabilities(ring)
        await sdk.start_sensor_report(ring)
        try:
            for _ in range(10):
                batch = await sdk.wait_sensor_data(ring, timeout_s=5.0)
                print("batch:", batch.sequence_start, batch.frame_count)
                for sample in batch.samples:
                    print(sample.timestamp_ms, sample.accel_x, sample.gyro_x)
        finally:
            await sdk.stop_sensor_report(ring)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

items.title: Save 0x0605 to TXT
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

This example uses the direct-start behavior of V2.001.0002.0001.

import asyncio
import openzilo as sdk

ADDRESS = "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"


async def main() -> None:
    async with sdk.OpenZiloClient(address=ADDRESS) as ring:
        await sdk.get_device_capabilities(ring)
        await sdk.start_sensor_report(ring)
        try:
            with open("imu_0605.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                for _ in range(20):
                    batch = await sdk.wait_sensor_data(ring, timeout_s=5.0)
                    for i, sample in enumerate(batch.samples):
                        seq = batch.sequence_start + i
                        f.write(
                            f"{seq},{sample.timestamp_ms},"
                            f"{sample.accel_x},{sample.accel_y},{sample.accel_z},"
                            f"{sample.gyro_x},{sample.gyro_y},{sample.gyro_z}\n"
                        )
        finally:
            await sdk.stop_sensor_report(ring)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

items.title: Local software calibration
items.text:
OpenZilo computes, stores and applies calibration on the host. No calibration commands or parameters are written to the ring. The known legacy IMU/2 firmware is supported; unknown or incompatible contracts are rejected. Firmware upgrades are not required for this feature.

openzilo imu-calibrate accel
openzilo imu-calibrate quick
openzilo imu-calibrate full
openzilo imu-calibrate show
openzilo imu-calibrate reset
openzilo sensor-stream --calibrated --seconds 10

accel collects six signed gravity directions with the ring fixed in the charging case, then fits diagonal accelerometer biases/gains and validates new data on three distinct axes. An inverted attachment and arbitrary face order are supported. Release the case before pressing Enter; use a support if necessary. Do not remove and reattach the ring during the six faces. Each face settles for 2 seconds and records at least 5 seconds.

quick calibrates only gyro bias. Remove the ring from the case, keep it away from magnets, and lay it still, with paper support to prevent rolling. Three consecutive windows must have mean gyro ranges within 0.08 deg/s (up to 3 minutes), followed by a minimum 20-second bias recording and fresh independent validation. Charging, magnetic attachment and temperature conditions must not be confused with normal-use bias. There is no full-turn rotation.

full performs both stages and replaces the local file only when both pass. Cancellation, drift, failed validation or storage failure preserves the previous file. Use accel first and quick later to retain independent progress. Each action preserves any previously validated parameters of the other component. Unvalidated components remain uncorrected.

Original start_sensor_report, wait_sensor_data and default sensor-stream semantics remain unchanged. Software correction is explicit:

async with sdk.OpenZiloClient(address=ADDRESS) as ring:
    async with sdk.open_calibrated_imu_stream(ring) as stream:
        async for batch in stream:
            for sample in batch.samples:
                print(sample.timestamp_ms, sample.accel_g, sample.gyro_dps)
            print(batch.applied_components)

The context starts/stops reports, cleans up on errors/cancellation, and is invalid after reconnect. Use an exclusive IMU consumer on the connection. Custom transports must provide device_id= for profile binding. CalibratedImuBatch and CalibratedImuSample preserve sequences/counts/timestamps and contain new float tuples in g and deg/s, leaving raw objects untouched. CLI JSONL marks data_domain="software_calibrated", accel_unit="g", gyro_unit="deg/s", and applied_components. An accel-only profile does not subtract gyro bias.

For range R, raw signed counts convert by counts * R / 32768. Per-axis corrections are (accel_g - accel_bias_ug/1e6) * accel_scale_ppm/1e6 and gyro_dps - gyro_bias_udps/1e6. The six-face fit uses a diagonal ellipsoid with unit gravity magnitude, permitting small fixture tilt. Gravity is retained. There is no gyro gain fit, full cross-axis matrix, temperature compensation, orientation fusion or drift-free heading.

Sampling rejects gaps, clipping, movement and within-window drift. Initial thresholds are 0.008 g accel standard deviation, 0.06 g peak-to-peak, 0.3 deg/s gyro standard deviation, and first/second-half mean changes of 0.003 g / 0.15 deg/s. Accel-stage quality ignores gyro bias/noise. Independent acceptance thresholds are 0.015 g gravity-norm error and 0.15 deg/s mean gyro residual per axis. Thresholds are acceptance rules, not universal accuracy claims.

Profiles live next to CLI preferences under imu/<device_hash>.json, normally ~/.config/openzilo/imu/ on Linux. They record schema, input domain, units, device hash, model, exact firmware version, parameters, component validation flags and creation time. Unknown chip type is 0. Device/model/firmware/ranges must match; recalibrate after firmware upgrades. Corrupt profiles fail explicitly. Save uses a temporary file, sync and atomic replace. Override with imu-calibrate --profile FILE or sensor-stream --calibrated --calibration-profile FILE.

Public helpers include ImuCalibration, ImuCalibrationProfile, imu_device_key, imu_calibration_path, load_imu_calibration_profile, save_imu_calibration_profile, apply_imu_calibration, analyze_imu_static_window, collect_imu_static_window, fit_imu_six_face_calibration, fit_imu_gyro_bias, and validate_imu_calibration. Offline application requires original raw samples and rejects already-calibrated batch types.

Future firmware application must explicitly negotiate raw/corrected data, chip identity, storage and ownership. This SDK sends no calibration commands and refuses software streams when firmware advertises calibration feature ID 11, preventing double correction.

items.title: Installation and requirements
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Install Python and uv first.

Install the Python SDK and its Bluetooth and audio dependencies, then follow the quick start.

items.title: Install and import
items.text:
After installation, import the package:

import openzilo as sdk

This guide uses sdk as an alias for openzilo.

items.title: Dependencies
items.text:
Use uv to install the SDK from GitHub into your project:

uv add git+https://github.com/ziloai/OpenZilo.git

Run Python scripts with uv run python your_script.py. Without uv, install directly from GitHub:

python -m pip install git+https://github.com/ziloai/OpenZilo.git

For device commands, see the CLI guide:

uvx --from git+https://github.com/ziloai/OpenZilo.git openzilo shell

To decode recordings to WAV, install ffmpeg and make it available from the command line:

ffmpeg -version

Downloading raw recording bytes without decoding does not require ffmpeg.

items.title: Python
items.text:
• Python 3.11 or later is recommended.
  • The SDK uses asyncio. Call asynchronous BLE operations with await inside async def.
  • In PyCharm, select the same virtual environment where bleak was installed.

items.title: Windows
items.text:
• Windows 10 or 11 is recommended.
  • Enable Bluetooth and disconnect other applications using the ring.
  • If other devices can discover the ring but this computer cannot connect, toggle Bluetooth, disconnect other BLE tools, and restart advertising on the ring.

items.title: Ubuntu/Linux
items.text:
• bleak is installed with the SDK.
  • Linux generally requires BlueZ and permission for the current user to access Bluetooth.
  • For scan or connection permission problems, check discovery with your system Bluetooth tools first.

Recording-to-WAV conversion needs ffmpeg; live PCM uses the pcm extra. See audio decoding and live audio for the installation requirements.

items.title: Live audio
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Receive live Opus or PCM from button-triggered recordings. Use connect_ring() to connect and discover features, or call get_device_capabilities() after connecting an OpenZiloClient. Event fields are listed in data types.

Code snippets use import openzilo as sdk; ring is a connected client. See the quick start for a complete connection example.

items.title: Receive live recordings
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

connect -> subscribe with receive_live_audio_file -> hold the button, then release
        -> device streams Opus audio -> SDK unsubscribes -> save_audio_bundle

async with sdk.OpenZiloClient(address=ADDRESS) as ring:
    await sdk.get_device_capabilities(ring)
    recording = await sdk.receive_live_audio_file(
        ring,
        on_subscribed=lambda: print("Hold the ring button to record, then release"),
    )
    bundle = sdk.save_audio_bundle(
        file_index=0,
        data=recording.data,
        output_dir="audio",
    )
    print(bundle.play_path)

Live recording requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later. Live-only recordings are not stored and cannot be recovered after disconnection or loss. Simultaneous saving provides a device copy to download after saving finishes. Wait for on_subscribed before asking the user to record.

items.title: open_live_audio_stream(): PCM / Opus events
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later. V2.001.0002.0000 transfers files after recording has been saved and does not provide live audio. Live PCM also requires the pcm extra.

Install PCM decoding dependencies with uv add "openzilo[pcm] @ git+https://github.com/ziloai/OpenZilo.git". PyAV decodes in-process, without an ffmpeg executable. output="opus" needs only the base SDK.

async with sdk.open_live_audio_stream(
    ring,
    output="pcm",             # Default; "opus" is also available
    queue_size=64,
    timeout_s=60.0,
    recording_timeout_s=70.0,
) as stream:
    print("Subscribed; hold the recording button now")
    async for event in stream:
        if isinstance(event, sdk.LiveAudioStart):
            print(event.sample_rate, event.channels)
        elif isinstance(event, sdk.LivePcmFrame):
            # data is 16 kHz, 16-bit little-endian PCM; see event.pcm_config for channels.
            # Pass audio to another task for speech recognition or playback.
            application_queue.put_nowait(event)
        elif isinstance(event, sdk.LiveAudioEnd):
            print("Complete recording", event.sent_bytes)

Create application_queue in your application and read it promptly from another task; downstream handling is omitted here. If it fills, stop reception or handle it according to application needs. Do not run slow synchronous processing in the receive loop. Keep the async with block for cleanup on cancellation, break or exception. No extra 0x050F–0x0511 listeners are needed.

Events arrive in this order:

Event Meaning LiveAudioStart session_id, device recording time, sample_rate=16000, channels=1 or 2, and codec=3. LivePcmFrame PCM mode: session_id, sample_offset, sample_count=320, data, and pcm_config containing the actual channels, 16 kHz rate and 16-bit depth. LiveAudioData Opus mode: session_id, sequence, compressed byte_offset, and original Opus data. LiveAudioEnd Validated packet and byte counts at recording end. PCM mode drains the decoder first.

sample_offset starts at 0 and advances by 320 per frame, measured per channel. Divide by 16000 for audio-relative time, not host reception time. Mono frames contain 640 bytes; stereo frames 1280, without WAV headers. Channel count matches the device, with no denoising or mixing. stream.start is available after START; stream.end and stream.complete are set only after final validation and decoder drain.

Entering the context waits only for subscription confirmation. timeout_s limits subscription and waiting for START separately. recording_timeout_s limits reception after START; inter-packet waits are capped at five seconds. A recording is at most 60 seconds and a stream receives one recording; open a new context for the next one.

The application event queue holds 64 events by default. The raw notification queue holds 256 packets by default, configured by client receive_queue_size. Slow consumption or notification backlog raises ProtocolError; queues do not grow indefinitely or silently drop frames. Decoder state also uses memory. These local buffers cannot throttle the device.

Only a validated LiveAudioEnd confirms a complete recording. PCM already delivered can be followed by loss, disconnect, invalid END or decoding failure. Distinguish partial audio from a complete recording. Cancellation and early exit produce no successful END. Empty recordings may contain START and END without audio frames.

Missing PyAV or decoder initialization failure raises OpusDecoderUnavailable before subscription; decoding failure raises AudioDecodeError. Other protocol, device, timeout and transport exceptions match file reception. Context exit attempts unsubscribe; on failure it logs a warning. Reconnect before more audio or OTA operations. A stream cannot be reused or read by concurrent tasks.

Cancellation partway through a BLE write makes the client reject further writes to avoid leaving a partial protocol packet. Unsubscribe may also fail; reconnect. The SDK does not report this as successful cleanup.

See examples/live_pcm.py for a complete example.

items.title: receive_live_audio_file()
items.text:
Firmware version

This usage requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

Purpose: subscribe, receive one button-triggered live recording, then unsubscribe. Requires firmware V2.001.0002.0001 or later.

Signature:

recording = await sdk.receive_live_audio_file(
    ring,
    on_packet=None,
    on_subscribed=None,
    timeout_s=60.0,
    recording_timeout_s=70.0,
)

Arguments:

  • on_subscribed: called when the device confirms subscription; use it to prompt recording.
  • on_packet: called for each validated LiveAudioData, containing original Opus bytes. Whole-recording completeness is confirmed only when the function returns.
  • timeout_s: maximum seconds for subscription and waiting for recording start.
  • recording_timeout_s: total limit from START to END, with at most five seconds between packets.

Callbacks may be synchronous or asynchronous and should return quickly. The function assembles received Opus into a complete file. Slow callbacks can fill the bounded queue and fail reception; slow synchronous callbacks also block the event loop. For PCM, use open_live_audio_stream(output="pcm").

Returns LiveAudioRecording; its data is a complete OP2C file accepted by save_audio_bundle() or decode_audio_to_wav().

Exceptions:

  • Rejected subscription, such as insufficient ATT MTU, or an END error code: DeviceError.
  • Inconsistent session, sequence, offsets, END counts or device-reported drops: ProtocolError.
  • BLE disconnect while waiting: TransportError.

Notes:

  • Live-only mode does not store recordings on the device. Simultaneous saving permits downloading the device copy after completion.
  • The function attempts unsubscribe on exit, including error and cancellation. If a complete recording is received but unsubscribe fails, it still returns the recording and logs an openzilo warning. Reconnect before downloads or firmware updates.
  • Do not combine a live subscription with downloads, receive_auto_audio_file() or OTA.

Low-level set_live_audio_subscription(client, enabled) only toggles subscription; handle 0x050F–0x0511 yourself. Disabling it aborts live transmission, and disconnect clears the subscription.

items.title: Read device logs
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Inspect device log storage and read raw bytes in chunks. Feature discovery is not required.

Code snippets use import openzilo as sdk; ring is a connected client. See the quick start for a complete connection example.

items.title: get_log_storage() and read_log_chunk()
items.text:
storage = await sdk.get_log_storage(ring)
chunk = await sdk.read_log_chunk(ring, index=0, offset=0, size=256)
print(chunk.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))

read_log_chunk() returns raw bytes. Decode using UTF-8 or the firmware's actual log encoding.

items.title: Version migration and firmware differences
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Check API changes when upgrading the SDK and discover features again after changing firmware. SDK and firmware have separate version numbers; version ordering alone does not determine compatibility.

items.title: BLE write chunks and migration from 0.3.x
items.text:
The SDK writes NUS RX in chunks of at most 20 bytes, with a shorter final chunk when necessary. Applications do not configure this size, and it does not disable Windows, Bleak or system MTU negotiation. Incoming notifications need not be 20 bytes; PacketStream reconstructs packets from their headers.

Since 0.4.0, NusClient no longer accepts write_chunk_size. Remove it from custom transport code using 0.3.x:

# Old 0.3.x usage, no longer supported
# transport = sdk.NusClient(address=ADDRESS, write_chunk_size=20)

# 0.4.0
transport = sdk.NusClient(address=ADDRESS)
ring = sdk.OpenZiloClient(transport=transport)

items.title: Differences between firmware implementations
items.text:
When upgrading from V2.001.0002.0000 to V2.001.0002.0001, update your application for these changes:

  • Remote recording and settings: V2.001.0002.0001 adds start, stop, status and configuration of channels, bitrate, gain and duration. V2.001.0002.0000 has none of these APIs.
  • Live audio: V2.001.0002.0001 adds live Opus output, which the SDK can decode to PCM. V2.001.0002.0000 transfers files after recording is saved.
  • Recording format: V2.001.0002.0000 uses Speex. New recordings in V2.001.0002.0001 use mono/stereo Opus (OP2C), with stereo as the default. The SDK still decodes existing Speex files.
  • Save notification: V2.001.0002.0000 pushes 0x0505 after saving. V2.001.0002.0001 notifies with 0x050A, followed by file download. Continue using receive_auto_audio_file() for both.
  • IMU: V2.001.0002.0000 requires gesture mode first. V2.001.0002.0001 starts capture on 0x0601 and stops on 0x0603 or disconnect. Subscribe again after reconnecting.
  • Button and tap events: V2.001.0002.0001 removes recording/gesture mode switching; single presses only report events. Tap detection runs with the IMU subscription instead of maintaining separate background capture.

See remote recording, live audio, IMU and events for SDK usage.

items.title: Update firmware with the SDK
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Transfer an official application firmware package through Python and verify the version after reboot. Discover features first; see the firmware guide for downloads and device instructions.

Code snippets use import openzilo as sdk; ring is a connected client. See the quick start for a complete connection example.

items.title: Firmware updates
items.text:
Update requirements

Use the official OTA package specified in the release notes. Match the device model, hardware revision and starting firmware version. The SDK updates application firmware only, not the bootloader.

update_firmware() and ota-update update application firmware; inspect the installed command with openzilo ota-update --help. They do not update the bootloader. Use an official package listing your model and starting version. Back up recordings, stop recording, downloads and IMU reporting, and maintain power and connection. The update exclusively owns this connection until it finishes.

Firmware packaging now produces ring_sound-V2.001.0002.0001-prod-1234abcd.ota.zip with manifest.json, manifest.sig, and app.ota.bin. The manifest carries version, model, board, test/production profile, security version, allowed source versions, and payload size/SHA-256. The outer signature can reuse the firmware P-256 signing key. Obtain the verification public key independently through a trusted channel; a key supplied inside a download is not a trust anchor.

from pathlib import Path

bundle = Path("ring_sound-V2.001.0002.0001-prod-1234abcd.ota.zip").read_bytes()
public_key = Path("trusted-signing-public.pem").read_bytes()
metadata = sdk.inspect_firmware_bundle(bundle, trusted_public_key=public_key)
print(metadata.version, metadata.model, metadata.board)
async with sdk.OpenZiloClient(address=ADDRESS) as ring:
    info = await sdk.update_firmware(ring, bundle, trusted_public_key=public_key)

Display all verified metadata offline, without connecting to a ring:

openzilo ota-inspect ring_sound-V2.001.0002.0001-prod-1234abcd.ota.zip --public-key trusted-signing-public.pem
# Add --json for machine-readable output.

inspect_firmware_bundle() returns a FirmwareBundle whose manifest property is a fresh dictionary of all verified fields. Invalid signatures fail without a success marker. Successful inspection establishes package authenticity and integrity; device compatibility is checked before uploading.

openzilo ota-update --address ADDRESS ring_sound-V2.001.0002.0001-prod-1234abcd.ota.zip --public-key trusted-signing-public.pem

Board comparison ignores repeated / separators to support Zephyr qualifiers with a leading slash. Display and signature verification preserve the original metadata.

Offline checks cover signature, archive structure, lengths, digest and encryption header. Before OTA starts, the SDK checks device model, board and source version. An empty source_versions explicitly allows any starting version. Test bundles require allow_test_firmware=True or --allow-test-firmware. When a device cannot report its board, only an exact verified legacy profile may supply it. Currently this covers Open Zilo firmware V2.001.0002.0001-prod-7fd1dfc9, whose board is recorded in that build’s delivery metadata. Other unknown boards are rejected. Security-version enforcement and matching device encryption keys remain device checks: the SDK cannot decrypt or read rollback counters. Only the inner OTA bytes are transmitted, and the running version is still checked after reboot.

OTA accepts only this signed ZIP format and rejects raw BIN input. The target version and compatibility fields come from verified metadata; version, sha256, and expected_model overrides have been removed. The full runtime version, including debug/prod and commit suffixes, is compared after reboot. Updating to the already running version is rejected. See update_firmware.py for a runnable example.

Argument Meaning client / firmware Connected client and the complete package bytes. trusted_public_key Trusted PEM P-256 public key bytes, required for ZIPs. allow_test_firmware=False Explicitly permit test ZIPs. progress=None Synchronous (sent, total) callback in bytes, for transfer progress only. Device resume requests may skip an already received prefix. timeout_s=30.0 Timeout for a single check, transfer or reconnection operation. total_timeout_s=600.0 Total limit for preparation checks and transfer. reboot_timeout_s=90.0 Limit for reboot, reconnect and version verification after transfer confirmation.

Returns SystemInfo read after reboot and reconnection. The SDK returns successfully only after verifying device identity and the target version. 100% transfer or a BLE disconnect does not mean installation succeeded. Device rejection raises DeviceError; timeouts, transport failure and invalid responses raise TimeoutError, TransportError and ProtocolError. Cancellation does not withdraw received bytes; reconnect and read the version after failure.

See the firmware update guide for releases and recovery.

items.title: Protocol debugging utilities
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Work directly with protocol bytes for debugging and custom transports. Prefer the high-level feature APIs in applications. See the protocol reference for packet formats.

Code snippets use import openzilo as sdk; ring is a connected client. See the quick start for a complete connection example.

items.title: Protocol debugging utilities
items.text:
Application code normally does not need these directly.

packet_bytes = sdk.encode_packet(0x0101)
packet = sdk.decode_packet(packet_bytes)
crc = sdk.crc16_compute(packet.body)

Use PacketStream to reconstruct packets from BLE fragments:

stream = sdk.PacketStream()
for packet in stream.feed(chunk):
    print(packet.command, packet.body)

Use BinaryReader and BinaryWriter to read or build bodies:

body = sdk.BinaryWriter().u16(0).u32(0).build()
reader = sdk.BinaryReader(body)
error_code = reader.u16()

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Connect a ring, read its model, firmware and battery level, then disconnect. Install the SDK using the installation guide first.

items.title: Scan for a device
items.text:
Run the following command in your uv project and copy the device address from its output.

uv run openzilo scan

items.title: Connect and read device information
items.text:
Replace AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF with the scanned address. On macOS, use the UUID returned by scanning:

import asyncio
import openzilo as sdk

ADDRESS = "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"


async def main() -> None:
    ring = await sdk.connect_ring(address=ADDRESS)
    try:
        info = await sdk.get_system_info(ring)
        print(info.model, info.firmware_version, info.battery_percent)
    finally:
        await ring.disconnect()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

ring is a connected OpenZiloClient. High-level device functions take it as the first argument, for example sdk.get_system_info(ring).

items.title: Run the example
items.text:
Save the code above as connect.py, replace the device address, then run:

uv run python connect.py

The script prints the model, firmware and battery level, then disconnects. Next, discover device features or choose a feature guide from the home page.

items.title: Synchronize device time
items.text:
Device applicability

This document applies to OpenZilo Q.

Configure automatic replies to device time requests, or respond manually in your application. Feature discovery is not required.

Code snippets use import openzilo as sdk; ring is a connected client. See the quick start for a complete connection example.

items.title: Enable automatic time synchronization
items.text:
connect -> enable_time_sync -> keep the connection open

async with sdk.OpenZiloClient(address=ADDRESS) as ring:
    sdk.enable_time_sync(ring)
    await asyncio.sleep(60)

items.title: enable_time_sync() and send_time_response()
items.text:
enable_time_sync() registers an automatic handler that replies to device 0x0401 with 0x0402.

It can be enabled before connection. Requests received while connecting or reconnecting wait until that connection is ready. The SDK records reception time when the request arrives and generates send time immediately before writing under the write lock. Disconnect or connection failure cancels pending replies; old replies never reach a new connection. Repeated calls do not duplicate the handler. connect_ring(auto_time_sync=True) registers before connecting to catch requests immediately after notifications start.

sdk.enable_time_sync(ring)

Use send_time_response() for a manual reply:

await sdk.send_time_response(ring, request_time)

Take request_time from the device's 0x0401 body.
